About 8VC

8VC is a technology investment firm headquartered in Austin, TX.  We partner with entrepreneurs to build technology platforms that create long-term economic and societal value. 8VC was built by a team of entrepreneurs, engineers, investors, and philosophers who value operating experience and action, as well as new ideas and creative theories. We invest primarily in smart enterprise platforms across industries including financial services, healthcare, logistics, and Bio-IT, as well as horizontal platforms, which encompass core enterprise infrastructure (data, software, cloud, AI) and departmental SaaS. For more information, please visit http://8vc.com

About the Role

We are seeking a versatile IT System Administrator to join our TechOps team in San Francisco. The ideal candidate will possess a can-do attitude and a strong sense of ownership, akin to that of a site manager. This role requires flexibility to transition seamlessly between tactical user support and project execution.

What You’ll Do

  • IT Systems Management: Oversee the day-to-day management of IT systems and infrastructure to ensure smooth operations across the organization.

  • End-User Support: Provide technical support to end-users, including troubleshooting hardware and software issues, setting up new devices, and assisting with IT-related inquiries. 

  • Software and Application Management: Install, configure, and maintain software applications and licenses, including productivity tools, collaboration platforms, and business applications, to support the needs of the organization.

  • IT Training and Documentation: Provide training and support to end-users on IT systems and procedures, as well as develop and maintain documentation and knowledge base articles to facilitate self-service support.

What You Bring

  • Excellent Customer Service and communication skills.

  • Experience with Okta administration and automation.

  • Proficiency in Google Workspace/MS365 administration.

  • Familiarity with MDM administration and zero-touch deployment.

  • Strong network administration and troubleshooting skills.

  • Prior experience in SaaS operations management.

  • Proficiency in supporting both Mac and Windows systems.

We appreciate your interest in joining our team. If we find that your qualifications and experience align with the requirements of the position, we will be in touch to further discuss. However, due to the high volume of applications we receive, we regret that we may not be able to personally respond to all candidates.

Join our mission to build lasting technology platforms and create long-term economic and societal value.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - MeritFirst
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Apply Here

America is strongest when ability can rise

The right person can change the trajectory of a team, a company, or an entire field.

But most hiring systems are built to avoid mistakes, not to discover extraordinary upside. They rely on the credentials that are easiest to read: the right degree, the right previous employer, or the right personal network. These filters, while convenient, are often very poor proxies for what someone can actually do.

When exceptional ability is missed, the loss is larger than one denied opportunity. A company loses performance. Coworkers lose a force multiplier. Ideas and businesses that could have existed never get built. A country that mistakes pedigree for ability does not merely distribute opportunity unfairly, it leaves growth on the table.

History suggests that better talent allocation has been a major source of American growth. When capable people reach the work where they can contribute most, workers rise, companies become more productive, and the benefits can spread through new ideas, stronger teams, families, and communities.

MeritFirst is building the infrastructure to make that the default. We create objective, efficient ways for people to demonstrate critical thinking, problem-solving, adaptability, and execution - and help companies hire based on demonstrated ability rather than pedigree alone.

For the worker, that means upward mobility. For the company, better performance. At scale, it can mean national growth.

 

The role

MeritFirst’s product has to do something much harder than move information around: it has to create a signal that deserves to influence consequential decisions about people.

Candidates must trust that they have a fair opportunity to demonstrate what they can do. Employers must trust that the resulting signal predicts performance better than the credentials they already use. Earning that trust requires exceptional product judgment, rigorous measurement, and software that is reliable, explainable, and built with care.

We’re looking for Software Engineers to help build that system from first principles. You will work directly with our founder, product team, candidates, and employers to shape and build the MeritFirst platform - from the candidate experience and assessment engine to employer workflows, evaluation systems, and the infrastructure beneath them.

This is not a role where a roadmap arrives fully specified. You will help determine what should exist, reduce ambiguous problems to their essential parts, ship the first version, observe how it behaves in the real world, and improve it quickly.

One day you may be designing a new assessment experience. The next, you may be debugging an edge case in production, working through an evaluation methodology with an assessment expert, simplifying an employer workflow, or deciding which manual process should become software.

AI gives engineers extraordinary new leverage, and we intend to use it. But our standard is not code that looks plausible or was produced quickly. It is a system we understand, can explain, can test, and can trust.

We expect our engineering team to have deep technical foundations while using modern tools to multiply judgment not replace it.

 

What you’ll build over time

The responsibilities below describe the full mandate of the engineering function over time, not a day-one checklist for one person.

You will begin by taking ownership of the highest-leverage product and technical problems, shipping directly to users, and developing a deep understanding of where software can most improve the candidate-to-hire loop. From there, you will help build the systems and engineering team that allow MeritFirst to scale.

  • Build the core product. Create candidate and employer experiences that make it easy to demonstrate ability, understand the resulting signal, and act on it.

  • Build a flexible assessment platform. Develop the primitives that allow us to create, deliver, evaluate, and continuously improve rigorous assessments and realistic work challenges across many kinds of roles.

  • Own problems end to end. Move from understanding the user and shaping the product through system design, implementation, deployment, observation, and iteration. You will own outcomes, not tickets.

  • Turn difficult human workflows into excellent software. Work closely with assessment experts, operators, and users to understand what should be automated, what should remain human, and how the two should fit together.

  • Build evaluation systems worthy of trust. Make results consistent, interpretable, auditable, and resistant to gaming. Design appropriate human review, testing, and safeguards into systems that affect real careers.

  • Close the learning loop. Connect assessment performance, employer decisions, and on-the-job outcomes so the product becomes more useful and predictive over time.

  • Use AI where it earns its place. Apply models where they materially improve assessment creation, evaluation, or the candidate and employer experience - and build the evaluations and guardrails required to know whether they are actually working.

  • Make trust a technical requirement. Treat reliability, security, privacy, accessibility, and candidate experience as foundational product properties rather than cleanup work.

  • Strengthen the technical foundation. Improve architecture, testing, observability, performance, and developer velocity where the business requires it - without prematurely building infrastructure we do not yet need.

  • Set the engineering standard. Establish the technical judgment, operating habits, and quality bar that future engineers will inherit. Help us identify and recruit the people who should join you.

 

Who will thrive here

You may have been an early engineer, technical founder, or senior individual contributor. You may have built an ambitious product at a startup, owned a critical system at scale, made meaningful open-source contributions, or developed exceptional ability outside a conventional path.

Your exact background matters less than evidence of unusual technical ability, product judgment, and ownership.

You will likely thrive here if:

  • You have built and operated meaningful production software, not only prototypes or narrowly bounded features.

  • You have exceptional technical foundations and can reason from first principles when existing abstractions stop helping.

  • You can move fluidly between shaping the product, designing the system, writing the code, reading unfamiliar code, and understanding what happens in production.

  • You have depth in at least one part of the stack and enough range to follow important problems wherever they lead.

  • You are an excellent debugger. When something behaves unexpectedly, you form hypotheses, follow evidence, and keep going until you understand why.

  • You combine speed with judgment. You know when to build the simplest thing that works, when to invest in a foundation, and how to avoid both perfectionism and careless debt.

  • You have strong product instincts and care deeply about the person on the other side of the screen.

  • You have built production software both with and without AI assistance. You understand where these tools create extraordinary leverage and where they can conceal shallow reasoning, brittle code, or false confidence.

  • You treat AI-generated code like code written by someone you have never worked with: inspect it, test it, and take full responsibility for it.

  • You communicate clearly, disagree directly, and make technical tradeoffs legible to non-engineers.

  • You want your work to matter in the real world and care deeply about our mission.

 

This may not be the right role if

  • You want requirements, architecture, and priorities to be fully specified before you begin.

  • You prefer to remain within a narrow technical layer or consider product, user research, support, data work, or operations outside your job.

  • You measure engineering quality primarily by code volume, feature count, or how quickly something can be generated.

  • You rely on frameworks or AI tools without being able to explain, debug, and own the systems they help produce.

  • You reach for elaborate architecture before understanding the problem or finding evidence that the scale requires it.

  • You enjoy greenfield building but lose interest in operating, repairing, and improving what you ship.

  • You want an established engineering organization, mature infrastructure, and settled operating playbook.

  • You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5. We care about sustainable performance, but building an ambitious company from the ground up will sometimes require long days and exceptional intensity.

  • You are more interested in the idea of meritocracy - or the current excitement around AI - than the difficult technical work required to build something people can trust.

 

Logistics

We practice what we preach: our hiring process is designed to surface demonstrated ability, not reward pedigree or interview polish. We care far more about what you can do rather than where you went to school or which logos appear on your resume.

You’ll move from a short initial screen to a conversation with a team member, a deeper role-relevant technical exercise, and final-round conversations focused on technical judgment, product sense, ownership, and mutual fit.

We may ask you to work both with and without AI assistance. We are not testing nostalgia or typing speed - we want to understand your technical foundations, how you reason, and how you use modern tools without surrendering judgment.

Along the way, you’ll experience the MeritFirst product firsthand, giving you a chance to evaluate what we’re building - and whether you’re excited to help shape it!

Apply Here

jobs.title: Software Engineer - MeritFirst
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About MeritFirst

At MeritFirst, we’re on a mission to revolutionize how companies identify and evaluate talent, regardless of background. By rejecting outdated, unreliable proxies for capability and embracing objective, merit-based assessments, we are rebuilding the meritocratic infrastructure of opportunity from the ground up.

Role Overview

As a Software Engineer at MeritFirst, you’ll be responsible for developing, testing, and deploying software solutions that meet the needs of our users. You’ll take features from initial idea to live product. Your work will power real‑time assessments, AI workflows, and tools that hiring managers rely on to build excellent teams. You will help transform the way organizations discover and empower talent across industries, setting a new standard for merit-based hiring.

What You’ll Do

  • Own features end‑to‑end: work with our CEO, company partners, and candidate users to define scope and sketch UX.

  • Build with Next.js + TypeScript, wire up data in Postgres / Drizzle, ship on Vercel, and iterate.

  • Shape product direction: propose experiments, cut scope intelligently, and use data and feedback to guide future decisions.

  • Keep things fast and reliable: instrument analytics / telemetry, write tests, review PRs, and improve performance and developer ergonomics.

Qualifications

Must-Haves

  • Meaningful experience building production web apps withTypeScript / React / Next.js and Postgres (impact > exact years).

  • Ability to design clean DB schemas, write performant queries, and reason about cost.

  • Product mindset: enjoy clarifying the core problem and delighting users through UX polish.

  • Crisp communication: written and async, and a bias toward action and ownership over waiting for direction.

Nice‑to‑Haves

  • Experience with real‑time video or proctoring technology, AI/LLM pipelines, or large‑scale assessment platforms.

  • Passion for meritocracy and building products that broaden access to opportunity.

Why Join Us?

  • Autonomy: rapid growth with outsized ownership and scope.

  • Modern stack: TypeScript, Next.js, Postgres, Drizzle, Vercel, LLMs.

  • Meritocracy: We focus on real capabilities, not credentials. You’ll be assessed based on your skills and ability to execute, not the name of your school or employer.

  • Innovation: Work on cutting-edge projects that challenge the status quo and empower people to succeed.

  • Backed by the best: We’re funded by 8VC and Slow Ventures, with support from world-class builders like Joe Lonsdale and Sam Lessin who’ve helped scale some of the most influential tech companies of the last decade.

Our Process

We practice what we preach. Core to our thesis is that resumes, school names, and pedigree are poor proxies for capability. We want to see what you can actually do.

We have designed a hiring process that gives everyone a fair shot to showcase their skills through objective work samples.

The Steps:

  1. Assessment 1 (The Gateway): Linked here. Want to jump the line? You can start this right now. We prioritize candidates who have data on the board.

  2. Team Screen: A conversation with a member of our team to discuss your background, our company, and the results of your first assessment.

  3. Assessment 2 (The Deep Dive).

  4. Work Sample Debrief: A deep-dive interview where we discuss your approach to Assessment 2.

  5. Final Sync: A final conversation with one or more members of our team.

Important Note on Location:

We are an in-person team based in Austin, TX. We believe the speed of iteration required at this stage happens best when we are in the same room.

The "No Dead Ends" Guarantee:

Even if this specific role isn't the right fit - or if the location doesn't work out - your effort won't be wasted. By completing our assessments, you will create a verified profile in the MeritFirst Talent Network. This allows you to showcase your validated skills to other world-class companies in our ecosystem without having to apply from scratch.

jobs.title: Product Engineer - Thorin
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Title: Product Engineer

Location: San Francisco
Company: Thorin
Stage: Seed

About Thorin

Most enterprise software still depends on people to push work forward, and things constantly fall through the cracks. Thorin is building autonomous AI agents that understand the full context of your organization, reading across Slack, email, docs, and other work surfaces to proactively keep things on track without anyone having to remember to follow up.

The company was cofounded by Markus Zirn, co-founder of Workato, and Joe Lonsdale, co-founder of Palantir. We have strong venture backing and are focused on what AI can fundamentally change about how companies operate, not just incremental improvements to existing workflows.

About the Role

We're building an AI product for enterprise customers. We need someone who can own large pieces of it end to end.

You should be a strong frontend engineer (TypeScript, React) who ships fast and writes clean code. You should have real experience building AI-powered products at work or at home, but thinking hard about what new interaction patterns are possible when models get better. You should have good product taste and often-updated opinions about what to build, not just how.

What We’re Looking For

jobs.title: IT Administrator
jobs.descriptionHtml:
IT Administrator with 8VC Portfolio Company (Onsite, Dallas, TX)

Role Overview

We are seeking a skilled IT Administrator to support our U.S. team as we expand our operations. In this role, you will oversee all aspects of our information technology functions, ensuring data security, regulatory compliance, and the effective management of all IT domains. This is a full-time, onsite position based in Dallas, TX.

About Us

We are a U.S. defense company specializing in delivering advanced hardware solutions to address strategic challenges facing the United States and its allies. Our work is conducted in close partnership with government stakeholders, built on a culture of accountability, discretion, and execution.

Core Responsibilities

  • Manage day-to-day IT operations to ensure secure, reliable, efficient, and compliant office systems.

  • Coordinate IT activities with internal teams, external vendors, and third-party assessors.

  • Maintain and enhance our cybersecurity posture by implementing and maintaining controls aligned to NIST (800-171/53), ITAR, and CMMC Level 2 compliance standards.

  • Ensure ongoing compliance: keep the organization audit-ready, manage SSPs, and address cybersecurity gaps promptly.

  • Administer, expand, and secure U.S. systems, identities, endpoints, and access rights.

  • Enforce least privilege principles; onboard and manage user access, and maintain hardened systems.

  • Monitor security tasks, track deadlines, and deliver compliance objectives.

  • Develop and update IT policies, processes, and documentation to support company growth.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain ongoing security, compliance, and audit readiness for all IT systems.

  • Uphold a strong, defensible security posture for U.S. government work.

  • Ensure all systems and data adhere to federal cybersecurity standards.

What You Bring

  • Exceptional organizational and ownership skills with strong attention to detail.

  • Sound judgment and reliability in a fast-paced, high-accountability environment.

  • Clear communicator with both technical and non-technical senior stakeholders.

  • Experience with or supporting DoD/U.S. government regulated environments.

  • 5+ years in IT support, systems administration, or similar roles.

  • Ability to work onsite in Dallas, TX.

Preferred:

  • Active U.S. Government Security Clearance.

Why This Role Matters

This position is fundamental to maintaining secure, compliant operations with U.S. government partners. Your expertise will help build the infrastructure and safeguards that empower our team to perform impactful work of national importance in a high-trust environment.

jobs.title: Founding Growth Operator - MeritFirst
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Apply Here

America is strongest when ability can rise

The right person can change the trajectory of a team, a company, or an entire field.

But most hiring systems are built to avoid mistakes, not to discover extraordinary upside. They rely on the credentials that are easiest to read: the right degree, the right previous employer, or the right personal network. These filters, while convenient, are often very poor proxies for what someone can actually do.

When exceptional ability is missed, the loss is larger than one denied opportunity. A company loses performance. Coworkers lose a force multiplier. Ideas and businesses that could have existed never get built. A country that mistakes pedigree for ability does not merely distribute opportunity unfairly, it leaves growth on the table.

History suggests that better talent allocation has been a major source of American growth. When capable people reach the work where they can contribute most, workers rise, companies become more productive, and the benefits can spread through new ideas, stronger teams, families, and communities.

MeritFirst is building the infrastructure to make that the default. We create objective, efficient ways for people to demonstrate critical thinking, problem-solving, adaptability, and execution - and help companies hire based on demonstrated ability rather than pedigree alone.

For the worker, that means upward mobility. For the company, better performance. At scale, it can mean national growth.

 

The role

Tests only matter if the right people take them and companies act on the results. A test creates signal; a network turns that signal into opportunity.

We’re looking for a hands-on Growth Operator to build that system. You will identify job categories where MeritFirst can become the best place to discover talent and attract exceptional candidates. You will turn real work into compelling assessments, build flagship programs and competitions around them, and work with companies to convert demonstrated ability into interviews, offers, and successful hires.

This is not a conventional growth-marketing or internal recruiting role. You will own the operating loop - from role selection and candidate acquisition through programs, employer activation, matching, and placement - and then turn what works into a repeatable growth engine.

This is a zero-to-one builder role. One day you may be selecting the next role category for MeritFirst to enter. The next, you may be recruiting candidates, refining a challenge with a domain expert, producing an event, convincing a hiring leader to interview someone they would normally overlook, or analyzing why strong candidates are dropping out of the funnel.

You will do the work, learn quickly, and build the playbook as you go.

 

What you’ll build over time

The responsibilities below describe the full mandate of the growth function over time, not a day-one checklist for one person.

You will start by identifying the highest-leverage wedge, owning candidate-to-hire loops end to end, and learning what works. From there, we will build the systems, partnerships, and team that allow us to expand.

We expect the initial focus to be narrow: choose one or two role categories, launch a remarkable candidate program, and turn demonstrated ability into real interviews and hires. You are not expected to do everything at once or alone. You are expected to determine what matters first, make it work, and build from there.

  • Choose the markets we enter. Identify role categories with meaningful employer demand, large pools of overlooked talent, and skills that can be demonstrated objectively.

  • Activate employer demand. Build relationships with founders, hiring managers, and talent leaders. Secure real opportunities and help companies understand how MeritFirst’s signal should inform their hiring decisions.

  • Build the candidate network. Find and activate exceptional people through communities, referrals, partnerships, content, schools, trade programs, creators, and channels that do not look like conventional recruiting.

  • Create ways for people to prove themselves. Work with our product team, assessment experts, hiring managers, and exceptional practitioners to turn popular roles into rigorous, efficient assessments and realistic work challenges.

  • Build flagship programs. Create competitions, cohorts, showcases, and in-person or online events that ambitious candidates want to participate in - and that employers pay attention to.

  • Make placements happen. Turn strong assessment performance into curated introductions, interviews, offers, and successful hires. Stay close enough to candidates and companies to understand what works after the introduction.

  • Build the growth flywheel. Turn placements into referrals, case studies, employer advocates, candidate ambassadors, and organic demand for the next program.

  • Measure the full funnel. Track candidate source, assessment completion, qualification, interview, offer, acceptance, retention, employer repeat rate, and candidate experience. Optimize for outcomes, not registrations or event attendance.

  • Productize what works. Some of the early work will be manual. Your job is to identify which parts should become software, systems, partnerships, and repeatable operating playbooks.

 

Who will thrive here

Your exact background matters less than evidence of your ability to influence people to take action and produce measurable outcomes.

You will likely thrive here if:

  • You are an unusually high-agency generalist who operates with extreme ownership and a maniacal sense of urgency.

  • You can move between strategy, growth, partnerships, recruiting, operations, and storytelling.

  • You have built something from zero - not merely operated a mature channel or inherited an existing playbook.

  • You can persuade both an exceptional candidate to bet on a new platform and a skeptical hiring leader to act on a new signal.

  • You have strong taste for programs, competitions, events, and experiences people genuinely want to join.

  • You are analytically rigorous and willing to kill exciting ideas that do not produce interviews and hires.

  • You are comfortable doing unscalable work before you know what should become scalable.

  • You treat candidate trust and experience as product requirements.

  • You write clearly, communicate directly, and can represent MeritFirst’s mission with conviction.

  • You care deeply about finding exceptional people whom existing systems fail to recognize.

 

This may not be the right role if

  • You prefer clean functional boundaries or consider certain work beneath you.

  • You want an established team, budget, brand, and operating playbook.

  • You primarily want to run paid acquisition, lifecycle marketing, or a conventional demand-generation funnel.

  • You are more interested in the idea of meritocracy than the difficult operational work required to make it real.

  • You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5. We care about sustainable performance, but building something ambitious from the ground up will require long days, unusual hours, and exceptional intensity.

 

Logistics

We practice what we preach: our hiring process is designed to surface demonstrated ability, not reward pedigree or interview polish. We care far more about what you can do rather than where you went to school or which logos appear on your resume.

You’ll move from a short initial exercise to a conversation with a team member, a deeper role-relevant exercise, and final-round conversations focused on judgment, ownership, and mutual fit.

Along the way, you’ll experience the MeritFirst product firsthand, giving you a chance to evaluate what we’re building - and whether you’re excited to help shape it!

Apply Here

lists.content: Join our global legal team to safeguard and develop 1inch’s intellectual property portfolio while supporting M&A, group reorganizations, corporate governance and wider corporate legal needs. You will structure protections across our technology stack, coordinate intellectual property matters in strategic transactions and oversee day-to-day corporate legal documentation. Working with engineering, IT, finance and marketing teams across multiple jurisdictions, you will help protect our innovations and support the compliant, efficient evolution of our group structure.

• Manage and develop the global intellectual property portfolio, including patents, trademarks and trade secrets.
  • Advise on open-source licensing, software intellectual property and brand protection, and train teams on related rights, risks and safeguards.
  • Establish internal intellectual property registration, review and risk procedures, coordinating global filings, enforcement and oppositions with external counsel.
  • Advise on intellectual property structuring in group reorganizations and corporate transactions, including due diligence, integration and post-closing matters.
  • Draft and negotiate intellectual property assignments, licences and transition agreements, and assess related risks in strategic transactions.
  • Coordinate cross-border legal input with internal stakeholders and advisers.
  • Draft and review commercial, vendor and procurement contracts, including NDAs, service agreements and licensing agreements.
  • Support entity management, governance filings, director and shareholder resolutions, board and shareholder processes, intercompany arrangements and funding documentation.
  • Maintain legal-entity databases and document repositories, monitor relevant legal developments and support policies, controls and group-wide compliance with applicable corporate laws and regulations.
  • Collaborate with engineering, IT, finance and marketing teams, educate business stakeholders and help scale legal operations and knowledge-sharing while providing clear advice under time pressure.

• You have at least seven years of legal experience, with a focus on intellectual property.
  • You have managed patent strategy and portfolio development, working with engineers to identify patentable innovations, prepare technical disclosures and guide applications through national and international filing procedures.
  • You have a proven record of supporting M&A and group reorganizations from an intellectual property perspective.
  • You are familiar with global entity structuring, general corporate contracts and governance.
  • You have a strong command of intellectual property law across jurisdictions, particularly Dubai local law and US Patent law.
  • You can connect high-level strategy with detailed delivery, develop pragmatic solutions through weighted risk analysis and translate legal obligations into operational processes and controls.
  • You can navigate legal ambiguity in fast-changing technical environments and manage multiple important initiatives under time pressure.
  • You bring strong critical-thinking, synthesis and communication skills, with the ability to persuade and influence internal and external stakeholders.
  • You are collaborative, practical and solutions-oriented, and can balance legal risk with commercial realities.
  • You are a proactive self-starter who can work autonomously across time zones.

• Experience combining law-firm practice with an in-house role at a technology company.
  • Experience developing internal frameworks for intellectual property identification and inventor-contribution workflows in a scaling technology organization.
  • Experience leading the patent-prosecution lifecycle, including prior-art searches, claim drafting, office-action responses and coordination with local agents in jurisdictions such as the USPTO and EPO.
  • Familiarity with crypto, DeFi or open-source ecosystems.

lists.content:
Lead our infrastructure and platform engineering function and evolve it towards AI-driven, progressively autonomous operations.

You’ll lead the team responsible for the cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes environments, CI/CD systems, observability platforms and developer capabilities that power the 1inch platform and broader DeFi ecosystem. You’ll define and deliver a platform strategy that improves reliability, scalability, security, developer experience and operational efficiency.

You’ll apply Cursor AI and agentic automation across the platform lifecycle from infrastructure provisioning and deployment to monitoring, troubleshooting, optimisation and incident response. You’ll establish operational feedback loops and develop controlled self-healing capabilities that detect problems, identify likely causes and execute safe remediation.

You’ll ensure automation operates within defined permissions, approval requirements, audit trails, rollback mechanisms and security policies. This role combines strategic leadership, technical judgement, people management and close collaboration with Product, Engineering, Security, Compliance and IT.

• Define and execute the DevOps and platform engineering strategy, aligning the platform roadmap with company, product and engineering priorities.
  • Lead, mentor and grow the team through hiring, performance management, career development and succession planning.
  • Establish clear ownership, engineering standards, operational processes and governance while building a culture of accountability, automation, reliability, security and continuous improvement.
  • Own the architecture and operation of cloud-native infrastructure, Kubernetes, networking, storage and shared platform services, improving scalability, resilience, standardisation and operational simplicity.
  • Apply infrastructure-as-code, policy-as-code, automation-first and controlled-change principles while overseeing capacity planning, cost optimisation, technology selection and strategic vendor relationships.
  • Embed Cursor AI and agentic automation across provisioning, CI/CD, release engineering, observability, troubleshooting, capacity planning and cost optimisation.
  • Build controlled self-healing mechanisms that detect anomalies, identify likely causes, execute approved remediation, verify recovery and learn from outcomes.
  • Provide self-service infrastructure, deployment capabilities, reusable tooling, paved paths and AI-assisted workflows, measuring agents for safety, accuracy, cost, auditability, remediation success and reduction of manual toil.
  • Define and enforce reliability, observability and security standards across infrastructure, CI/CD and platform services, including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, resilience testing, incident management, access controls, secrets, encryption, vulnerability management and software supply-chain security.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Security, Compliance and IT to establish platform guardrails, risk controls, audit evidence and ownership boundaries, and represent platform performance, risks, investment needs and progress in executive discussions.

    •

• You have 10+ years of experience in DevOps, platform engineering, infrastructure engineering or SRE, including strong production experience with cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, distributed systems and high-availability environments.
  • You have 5+ years of experience leading platform or DevOps teams and have introduced AI-assisted engineering practices across a technical organisation.
  • You have advanced practical experience using Cursor Agent, Cursor CLI and Cloud Agents to design, implement, test, review and document infrastructure, platform services, operational tooling and automation.
  • You have used Cursor AI with Terraform, Kubernetes manifests, policy-as-code, configuration management and platform repositories while maintaining testing, peer-review and controlled-change requirements.
  • You have integrated Cursor CLI or Cloud Agents into CI/CD workflows for code review, test generation, configuration validation, security checks, documentation, refactoring and pipeline-failure remediation.
  • You can use Cursor AI to analyse telemetry and operational code, improve runbooks, investigate incidents, generate remediation changes and develop controlled self-healing mechanisms with verification and rollback.
  • You can coach engineers in effective Cursor workflows and measure adoption through delivery lead time, change-failure rate, automation coverage, operational toil, remediation quality and developer satisfaction.
  • You hold a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology or a related field, or have equivalent practical experience.

• Experience operating blockchain, Web3 or DeFi infrastructure.
    Experience with LLMOps, MLOps, model evaluation or operational agent orchestration.
  • Experience with multi-cloud, service mesh, event-driven or large-scale microservices environments.
  • Experience applying FinOps and predictive capacity optimisation at scale.
  • Familiarity with ISO 27001, SOC 2 or comparable frameworks, or relevant cloud, Kubernetes, Terraform, SRE, security, FinOps or AI/ML operations certifications.

This is not an active vacancy. Instead, we're building a network of exceptional backend engineers with a focus on Typescript or Golang and solid Web3 experience, who have successfully completed our interview process and are ready to join 1inch when new positions become available.

Our engineering needs evolve rapidly, and we're always looking to connect with exceptional individuals who want to help shape the future of DeFi. We look for engineers with a high-agency, "Get Stuff Done" mindset and an unrelenting passion for decentralised innovation.

We also embrace AI as a force multiplier for engineering, and value developers who thoughtfully leverage AI-powered tools to accelerate development, improve code quality, and solve complex technical challenges.

Successful candidates who pass the interview process will join our Pre-Qualified Talent Network. This means that when a suitable position becomes available, you'll be among the first people we consider, allowing us to move quickly through the final hiring stages and, where appropriate, straight to an offer.

• Build, extend, and operate backend services and APIs that power 1inch products and internal platforms
  • Improve scalability, reliability, maintainability, and developer experience across backend systems
  • Design and implement integrations with smart-contract platforms, blockchain data sources, and external services
  • Contribute to observability, monitoring, incident response, and post-mortem processes
  • Optimise backend services for performance, resilience, and operational efficiency
  • Collaborate closely with product, blockchain, and infrastructure teams to deliver reliable distributed systems
  • Participate in code reviews, testing workflows, and engineering best practices across the development lifecycle
  • At senior level, own services end-to-end, define technical direction, and mentor other engineers

• Professional experience building and operating backend systems in production environments
  • Strong proficiency in Golang, Typescript or another backend/systems programming language with practical concurrency and performance knowledge
  • Solid understanding of system design fundamentals including services, data flows, reliability, and maintainability
  • Familiarity with blockchain platforms, smart contracts, transaction handling, and on-chain integrations
  • Experience working with containerised services and modern deployment practices
  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work effectively in fast-paced engineering environments
  • Ability to balance technical quality, scalability, and operational reliability
  • At senior level, experience owning projects end-to-end and contributing to architectural decision-making

• Experience working with multiple blockchain networks or non-EVM ecosystems
  • Familiarity with on-chain data indexing, observability tooling, or protocol debugging systems
  • Experience building performance-sensitive systems such as routing engines, risk controls, or high-throughput pipelines
  • Experience working within fintech, crypto, or other correctness-critical domains
  • Exposure to distributed systems or low-latency infrastructure architectures

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Agent Platform
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Arca

Arca is a wealth management firm built from the ground up with AI. Most people get financial advice that's reactive: an annual check-in, a plan that's a document instead of a living thing, a relationship where you're one of three hundred clients your advisor is trying to remember. We think that's backwards. The kind of service that used to require a team of specialists behind you, the kind that makes you feel like the only person in the room, should be available to far more than the ultra-wealthy.

So we're building it. We're not SaaS — we are the wealth management business, rebuilding it from the inside with AI. Our platform is an Iron Man suit for advisors: it takes over the low-leverage work so they can focus on what actually requires a human, showing up with empathy, context, and judgment. Underneath, it keeps a living understanding of each client. It remembers the thing you mentioned once, six months ago. It notices when your life changes — a new job, a new kid, a market shift — and adjusts before you think to ask. You won't see the technology. You'll just notice your advisor seems to know you better than any financial professional ever has.

That's the product we're growing: client by client, on the strength of the experience itself. We started by acquiring firms managing over $1B in client assets, which gave us real advisors, real clients, and real financial outcomes to build against from day one. But acquisition was the starting line. The bet is that an advisor backed by this platform delivers something good enough that clients come to us on their own.

It's a $20T market, and we think it's ready to be rebuilt.
— Rron, CEO

The receipts

  • Stage: Series A, $64M raised

  • Backed by: General Catalyst, Index Ventures, Venrock

  • Board & Advisors: Former CEO of Vanguard, Former CFO of Schwab, Founder of Altruist, Morgan Housel (author of The Psychology of Money)

The team

We’re small on purpose. We’re a team of 12 based out of NYC and we’re engineering heavy with 8 engineers. We hail from high growth startups like Stripe, Ramp, Rippling, Plaid, Doordash, & Glean.

We’re fully in-office in Flatiron, five days a week—lunch together, coffee breaks, basketball games, happy hours.


The role

As a Member of Technical Staff focused on Applied AI, you’ll own our AI stack end to end. One framing we keep coming back to: agents are the primary users of our system of record. Everything we build (the data models, the APIs, the UI) has to work for a non-human user that operates at scale, across every client, all the time. That’s a different design constraint than most teams are used to.

What you’ll build (and own)

  • A general agent capable of complex, multi-step tasks — planning, sandboxed code execution, web search, retrieval — that powers a "do anything" experience for advisors.

  • Ambient agents that act on behalf of clients and advisors: triaging email, processing meetings, drafting communications, surfacing what needs attention before anyone asks.

  • The agent harness that orchestrates LLMs, context, tools, retrieval, and business logic into something coherent and reliable.

  • Generative UI and human-in-the-loop interfaces where the agent and advisor genuinely collaborate, not just take turns.

  • Evaluation infrastructure that holds two bars at once: high-correctness financial data and subjective, judgment-heavy tasks.

Example problems you’d work on

These aren’t hypothetical problems; we’re actively working on versions of all of these.

  • Human / AI collaboration that actually works in practice. An advisor is mid-call when the agent surfaces a multi-step recommendation: rebalance, adjust the savings rate, revisit the estate plan. The advisor takes two steps and overrides the third. Now what? How does the agent update its model of what this advisor wants, present reasoning the advisor can relay without sounding scripted, and learn over time what to do autonomously versus flag? This is the flywheel: the tighter the collaboration, the more the agent can take on.

  • Memory systems that know a client the way a great advisor does. A good advisor remembers that a client gets anxious when markets drop, cares more about the kids' college fund than their own retirement, and prefers plain-English summaries. Building memory that captures and evolves this understanding across years—and surfaces the right context at the right moment—is genuinely hard. The challenge is knowing what to retrieve, what's still relevant, and how to represent a person's relationship to money in a way an agent can use.

  • Generative UI as an agent architecture problem. When an agent views and updates the advisor's screen in real time—rendering scenarios, adjusting visualizations mid-conversation, surfacing recommendations inline—the UI is constantly changing. The challenge is how the agent manages state across those changes and how you keep the experience from feeling unpredictable. When the visualization shows a client's actual retirement savings, the advisor can't be surprised by their own screen.

  • Evaluations that work for financial services. Most evals are built for tasks with a single right answer. Financial advice isn’t like that; the same recommendation can be right for one client and wrong for another, and “correct” often depends on context the eval harness doesn’t have. You’ll build evaluation infrastructure that can hold two different bars simultaneously: high-accuracy financial data where errors have real consequences, and judgment-heavy tasks where the right answer is subjective and the stakes are relational. Add to this the compliance requirements of financial services, where auditability isn’t optional and infrastructure has to handle large, constantly changing datasets where a stale answer can be as harmful as a wrong one.

The kind of person who thrives here

You’re excited by ownership, ambiguity, and building things that matter.

  • You're comfortable where "correct" isn't always obvious. Financial advice isn't deterministic, and neither is evaluating it. You're energized by probabilistic systems and rigorous about the evaluation infrastructure that tells you whether you're improving—you trust experimentation more than your first instinct.

  • You're ambitious in a way specific to this work. You're building agents that touch real retirement savings and estate plans. A hallucination here isn't a product bug; it's a wrong answer that affects someone's financial future. That consequence makes you more careful, not slower.

  • You move fast, and you know speed and reliability aren't in tension here. An agent that behaves differently in production than in eval is a liability. You treat evaluation and iteration as part of shipping, not steps that come after.

  • You have taste, and a high bar for what that means here. You spot AI slop instantly and won't let it through review. You know "tech debt vs. shipping" is a false tradeoff and act accordingly—leaving systems better instrumented and better understood than you found them.

  • You’re someone people actually want to be in the room with. This is a 12-person team, one office, five days a week, working on problems that don’t have clean answers. The people who thrive here to argue about agent architecture at lunch and then run an eval together in the afternoon. Kind, direct, and low-ego, you can give candid feedback without being an asshole, and you’re genuinely energized by this environment (not just tolerant of it).

Why now is the moment to join

This is a narrow window with unusually high leverage.

  • We just came out of stealth, and we're growing fast. The team is intentionally small, the equity reflects that, and the ceiling is high. You'd be joining early enough that the work you do now directly shapes what the company becomes and what's possible next.

  • The advisor-facing product is being defined right now, by a small team that talks to advisors every day. We've just brought on our second firm—the real inflection point, where we start separating what generalizes from what was bespoke. The patterns you set become the foundation for every acquisition that follows.

  • The consumer product is a blank page. We've never built directly for consumers until now—no legacy, no template. Whoever takes this on defines what the experience even is.

  • The hard part is behind us, which means the interesting part is starting. The platform is live, the concept is proven, advisors have moved real client assets onto it. The work now is scaling a working system across four or five acquisitions this year—workflows, data, agents, reliability under real load.

As Chief of Staff to the CEO, you are the company's force multiplier. At this stage, a lot of what matters most doesn't fit neatly inside one function, and a lot of it has no owner yet, so it lands on you. You'll run how the company operates day to day, own the cross-functional work that matters most, turn decisions into system, and explore new verticals.

Our mission is to automate the operational substrate of financial services so the human moments can feel extraordinary.   • The things that don't have an owner yet. A lot of what will matter most a year from now has no team and no title today: new growth channels, new functions to stand up, new ways to finance and fuel the business, the next vertical worth a serious look. You take these from a vague question to something that runs without you: sometimes a function you hand to a team, often a system that runs on its own. This is where a lot of your time goes, and where the role has the most room to grow.

  • Finding leverage across the company. With a small team and a lot of work, much of your value is making everyone else faster. You find the manual, repetitive work that's eating people's time and build a better way to do it, and you teach people to do it for themselves.

The kind of person who thrives here

You’re excited by ownership, ambiguity, and building things that matter.

  • You're an operator who gets stuff done. Given a vague, half-defined problem, you come back with it resolved rather than with a list of questions. You see the details through to the end, and you don't call something done until it actually works.

  • You're AI-pilled. You already use AI for hours a day, and it's changed how you work and what you think one person can do. Faced with a new problem, your first instinct is to reach for it, and you're hands-on enough to build something real rather than just ask someone else for it. If it comes to it, you'll dig into the code and ship a PR yourself. You'd reach for a better system before you'd reach for another hire.

  • You hold a high bar because of what's at stake. This is people's real money: their retirement, their savings, the plans they have for their families, in a highly regulated industry where mistakes have real consequences. You don't settle for good enough, and the stakes make you more careful, not slower.

  • You move fast, and you keep many things moving at once. You can hold a dozen unrelated threads without letting any of them drop, and you have a feel for which ones actually matter today and which can wait.

  • You’re someone people actually want to be in the room with. This is a 12-person team, one office, five days a week, working on problems that don’t have clean answers.  - You're AI-pilled. You already use AI for hours a day, and it's changed how you work and what you think one person can do. Faced with a new problem, your first instinct is to reach for it, and you're hands-on enough to build something real rather than just ask someone else for it. The platform takes the busywork that eats most advisors' days, so your time goes where it matters: sitting with a client, understanding what they're actually worried about, and coming back with advice that fits their life. And the clients are coming — we're ramping marketing, inbound is about to grow fast, and your job is to meet it.

You'll work out of our NYC office, next to the engineers building the tools you use. That's not a perk, it's the job. You're one of the first advisors on the platform, which means you shape it: you give product and engineering the unvarnished advisor's view of what's slow, what's missing, and what would make you faster, and you watch it get built.   • Shaping the platform. You sit with engineering and product and tell them the truth about what advisors actually need. You have direct influence over what gets built and in what order.

  • Growth that compounds. As marketing fills the funnel, you turn inbound interest into long-term relationships — and the patterns you set become the foundation every advisor after you builds on.

You're excited by ownership, ambiguity, and building things that matter.

  • You're a real planner, not a salesperson with a CFP. You've spent 5-10+ years advising high-net-worth clients and you think in plans, not products — retirement, tax, cash flow, the whole picture. You've handled the complicated cases: stock options, RSUs, concentrated equity, the comp structures that take real work to get right. CFP® (or well on your way) and Series 65 (or able to get it).

  • You actually want the technology to be good. Most advisors treat their tools as something to tolerate. You're the opposite — you're genuinely curious about what AI can take off your plate, and you'd rather tell an engineer exactly what's slowing you down than work around it for another year. You don't need to write code; you need strong opinions and the willingness to share them.

  • You build trust because the stakes are real. This is people's retirement, their kids' futures, the plans they've made for their families.   • You're someone people actually want to be in the room with. This is a small team, one office, five days a week, working on problems that don't have clean answers. The role

The infrastructure, backend systems, and developer experience that let a 12-person team ship agents into a regulated, high-stakes domain without slowing down.   • Core infrastructure and backend systems. The services, data stores, and APIs that everything else is built on—designed for a workload where non-human agents are the heaviest, most constant users. This is what lets the rest of the team move fast without the ground shifting under them.

  • Safe execution for agents. The sandbox where agents write and run code and take real actions, plus the controls that let them reach our backend and databases without doing damage—versioned SDKs, scoped permissions, rate limits, isolation.

  • Developer experience and internal efficiency. The build, test, deploy, and observability tooling that determines how fast eight engineers can ship.   • Performance and cost. The systems that keep agents fast and correct under real load, and keep our infrastructure spend sane as we scale across four or five acquisitions this year. An agent that's slow, flaky, or ruinously expensive to run isn't shippable.

  • Cloud agents that triage and fix bugs. With eight engineers shipping into a high-stakes domain, engineering time is our scarcest resource. Internal leverage that compounds across every acquisition.

  • Powering the M&A acquisition engine.   • Querying years of portfolio data at agent speed. Agents need to reason over years of portfolio performance history, and they need it instantly—without hammering the systems that keep the product running. You'll build the read paths, stores, and deep integrations with custodians and performance-reporting providers that let agents query deep history quickly while keeping our backend systems isolated and healthy.

  • Maturing our backend. The platform is live and proven; now it has to scale across four or five acquisitions this year. You'll level up the foundation—data warehouses, pipelines, and the core systems everything runs on—so it holds up as data volume and agent load grow.

The kind of person who thrives here

You’re excited by ownership, ambiguity, and building things that matter.

  • You think in systems and take ownership of the whole stack. You're happiest when you understand how something works end to end, and you instinctively leave infrastructure better instrumented and better understood than you found it.   • You move fast, and you know speed and reliability aren't in tension here. Advisors depend on what you build every day. Breaking prod isn't something you wait until Monday to fix.

  • You're someone people actually want to be in the room with. This is a 12-person team, one office, five days a week, working on problems that don't have clean answers. Kind, direct, and low-ego, you can give candid feedback without being an asshole, and you're genuinely energized by this environment (not just tolerant of it).

This is a narrow window with unusually high leverage.

  • We just came out of stealth, and we're growing fast. The team is intentionally small, the equity reflects that, and the ceiling is high. You'd be joining early enough that the work you do now directly shapes what the company becomes and what's possible next.

  • The advisor-facing product is being defined right now, by a small team that talks to advisors every day. We've just brought on our second firm—the real inflection point, where we start separating what generalizes from what was bespoke. The patterns you set become the foundation for every acquisition that follows.

  • The consumer product is a blank page. We've never built directly for consumers until now—no legacy, no template. Whoever takes this on defines what the experience even is.

  • The hard part is behind us, which means the interesting part is starting. The platform is live, the concept is proven, advisors have moved real client assets onto it. The work now is scaling a working system across four or five acquisitions this year—workflows, data, agents, reliability under real load.

We’re fully in-office in Flatiron, five days a week—lunch together, coffee breaks, basketball games, happy hours. (For this role we are open to a remote hire!).

The Role

As Arca's first recruiter and recruiting lead, you'll be responsible for building our team and maintaining high talent density. We're not handing you a requisition list and a job board login; we're handing you the function. Right now, hiring happens because a founder or a hiring manager carves out time between everything else they're supposed to be doing. That doesn't scale and you're here to help fix that: build the pipeline, run the process, and close the people who will define what this company becomes.

You'll be recruiting for two very different worlds at once. On one side, technical talent — engineers who can operate with the ownership our product team already has. On the other, everything else: wealth advisors carrying real licenses and real client relationships, GTM and marketing hires shaping a brand that's barely a few months old, operators for functions that don't have a playbook yet. Most recruiters specialize in one lane. Here, you're building both, and building the muscle to add more as the company adds functions.

  • Pipeline and sourcing. Build and run full-cycle recruiting across everything we need, from engineers, product hires, GTM, ops, and beyond. You'll be empowered to connect with a wide breadth of candidates and leaders who will meet and raise the bar our current team set. You'll run the sourcing motion yourself, not just manage a pipeline someone else fills.

  • The hiring function itself. There's no process to inherit — you're building it: interview loops that predict who succeeds here, scorecards hiring managers trust, an ATS workflow build to scale. What you set up in the next few weeks/months is what every hire will experience.

  • Exceptional candidate experience. For most candidates, you're the first conversation they have with Arca, and the offer stage is often the last thing standing between a great candidate and a great hire. You will help create the experience and excitement people feel when they learn about Arca, and even more so when they decide the opportunity here is right for them.

  • Scaled recruiting. As hiring picks up, you build the muscle to keep pace with it. You'll bring in and manage external recruiters or agencies where they add leverage and where it makes sense, eventually building out the internal recruiting team you'll need. You're not just filling today's roles — you're building the function that fills next year's.

The kind of person who thrives here

You’re excited by ownership, ambiguity, and building things that matter.

  • You're a builder, not a coordinator. You're here to drive growth of our business by ensuring we have the right people. You don't ask for a headcount plan and a rubric — you build both while you're already sourcing candidates. You've stood up a recruiting function before, or you've been the person a founder leaned on to do it in all but title.

  • You can recruit technical talent for real. You know how to evaluate engineers, speak their language to earn their respect, and help close them when there are other options. While technical candidates won't be the only profile we are seeking, it'll be a big part of the job.

  • You're AI-pilled. You already use AI for hours a day, and it's changed how you work and what you think one person can do. Faced with a new problem, your first instinct is to reach for it, and you're hands-on enough to build something real rather than just ask someone else for it. You'd reach for a better system before you'd reach for another hire.

  • You’re someone people actually want to be in the (remote) room with. This is a 15-person team, working on problems that don’t have clean answers. Kind, direct, and low-ego, you can give candid feedback without being an jerk, and you’re genuinely energized by this environment (not just tolerant of it).

jobs.descriptionPlain:
Animoca Brands Corporation Limited (ACN: 122 921 813) is a Web3 leader that leverages tokenization and blockchain to deliver digital property rights to consumers, helping to establish the open metaverse and its associated network effects. Animoca Brands realizes its mission via three integrated business pillars: operating Web3 businesses to advance blockchain adoption with native projects such as Moca Network, Anichess, The Sandbox, Open Campus, NEOM Web3 initiatives, and a regulated stablecoin project in partnership with Standard Chartered and HKT; providing digital asset advisory services including tokenomics advisory, liquidity provisioning, and institutional research to help external Web3 projects grow; and investment management, with a portfolio of investments in over 540 companies including industry leaders Pudgy Penguins, Yuga Labs, Axie Infinity, Polygon, Consensys, Magic Eden, OpenSea, Dapper Labs, YGG, and many others.


About the Role:
 
We are searching for a Senior Associate to join our dynamic team to handle day-to-day financial operations and reporting for our diverse portfolio of entities, along with quarterly and month-end closing activities. You will handle traditional accounting duties while gaining unique exposure to Web3 accounting, digital assets, and cryptocurrency reconciliation.

About the Role:
 
We are searching for a Senior Associate to join our dynamic team to handle day-to-day financial operations and reporting for our diverse portfolio of entities, along with quarterly and month-end closing activities. You will handle traditional accounting duties while gaining unique exposure to Web3 accounting, digital assets, and cryptocurrency reconciliation.

lists.content:
• Liaise with external auditors for statutory audits, collate testing samples, and prepare accounting memos

  • Manage the full-set bookkeeping for up to 20 standalone entities across various jurisdictions (including Hong Kong, Middle East, United Kingdom, Korea, and Cayman Island etc.)

  • Handle daily accounting operations including monthly subsidiary funding and cost recharges

  • Ensure invoices are prepared correctly and accurately updated in the accounting system

  • Verify invoices and agreements to ensure the validity of supporting documents and proper authorization

  • Perform regular bank reconciliations to ensure all transactions are accurately recorded in the ledger

  • Manage Accounts Payable settled in cryptocurrency, ensuring crypto payments are properly recorded and reconciled with on-chain transactions

  • Perform ad hoc assignments, including but not limited to accounting standard interpretation and the development of accounting policies and procedures

  • Identify opportunities for process improvement and provide guidance or mentorship to junior team members

• Minimum 5 years of relevant experience, preferably with a mix of Big 4 audit and commercial accounting, less experience can be considered as a Senior Associate

  • QP candidate / CPA is a plus 

  • Proficiency in modern ERP systems (e.g. Oracle, NetSuite, or Expensify)

  • Experience with the Microsoft Office suite of programs is essential

  • Excellent written and spoken English

  • Good time management and an organized approach to tasks

  • Excellent attention to detail

  • Ability to take ownership and responsibility for assigned tasks

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team

  • A professional and positive attitude, remaining patient and calm under pressure

  • Willingness to learn and adapt in a fast-paced environment

Animoca Brands realizes its mission via three integrated business pillars: operating Web3 businesses to advance blockchain adoption with native projects such as Moca Network, Anichess, The Sandbox, Open Campus, NEOM Web3 initiatives, and a regulated stablecoin project in partnership with Standard Chartered and HKT; providing digital asset advisory services including tokenomics advisory, liquidity provisioning, and institutional research to help external Web3 projects grow; and investment management, with a portfolio of investments in over 540 companies including industry leaders Pudgy Penguins, Yuga Labs, Axie Infinity, Polygon, Consensys, Magic Eden, OpenSea, Dapper Labs, YGG, and many others.

About the Role:
As Assistant Manager, Group Reporting at Animoca Brands, you will play a pivotal role in helping drive the group’s consolidated financial reporting and audit processes in a dynamic, fast-evolving environment at the forefront of blockchain, digital assets, and gaming. You will be responsible for the preparation, review, and delivery of consolidated financial statements for the group, ensuring compliance with IFRS and all relevant regulatory requirements, and supporting the group audit process across a complex, multi-entity structure.

lists.content:
• Help drive the preparation and review of timely, accurate, and comprehensive consolidated financial statements for the group in accordance with IFRS, ensuring compliance with all relevant regulatory and internal requirements, and reflecting the unique aspects of digital assets, tokenomics, and virtual goods.

  • Help drive the group consolidation process, including the elimination of intercompany transactions, reconciliation of intercompany balances, and accounting for complex group structures, joint ventures, and associates.

  • Manage the end-to-end group audit process, acting as the primary point of contact for external auditors, coordinating audit deliverables, and ensuring timely resolution of audit queries across all group entities.

  • Review and analyze group-level financial results, including variance and trend analysis, and provide actionable insights and recommendations to senior management to support strategic decision-making.

  • Partner with regional and entity-level finance teams to ensure consistency and accuracy in financial reporting, and to help drive process improvements and best practices in group consolidation and reporting.

  • Develop, implement, and maintain robust internal controls and group reporting processes to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and compliance, particularly in relation to digital asset management and revenue recognition from gaming and blockchain activities.

  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior finance team members, fostering a culture of continuous learning and professional development in a high-growth, innovative environment.

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline; a Master’s degree is an advantage.

  •  Professional accounting qualification (e.g., CPA, ACCA, CA) is required.

  • Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in finance or accounting roles, including significant experience in financial reporting and audit (Big 4 or equivalent experience is highly valued).

  • Expert knowledge of IFRS and financial reporting standards, with a proven track record of managing complex reporting requirements—ideally with exposure to digital assets, gaming, or technology sectors.

  • Demonstrated experience with Netsuite or similar ERP/accounting systems is highly desirable

  • Advanced proficiency in Excel, including financial modeling, pivot tables, and advanced data analysis functions.

  • Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across all levels of the organization.

  • Experience in a fast-paced, high-growth, or entrepreneurial environment, and a genuine interest in blockchain, Web3, and digital entertainment, will be highly regarded.

About the Role:
 
We are searching for a Senior Associate to join our dynamic team to handle day-to-day financial operations and reporting for our diverse portfolio of entities, along with quarterly and month-end closing activities. You will handle traditional accounting duties while gaining unique exposure to Web3 accounting, digital assets, and cryptocurrency reconciliation.

lists.content:
• Liaise with external auditors for statutory audits, collate testing samples, and prepare accounting memos

  • Manage the full-set bookkeeping for up to 20 standalone entities across various jurisdictions (including Hong Kong, Middle East, United Kingdom, Korea, and Cayman Island etc.)

  • Handle daily accounting operations including monthly subsidiary funding and cost recharges

  • Ensure invoices are prepared correctly and accurately updated in the accounting system

  • Verify invoices and agreements to ensure the validity of supporting documents and proper authorization

  • Perform regular bank reconciliations to ensure all transactions are accurately recorded in the ledger

  • Manage Accounts Payable settled in cryptocurrency, ensuring crypto payments are properly recorded and reconciled with on-chain transactions

  • Perform ad hoc assignments, including but not limited to accounting standard interpretation and the development of accounting policies and procedures

  • Identify opportunities for process improvement and provide guidance or mentorship to junior team members

• 3 years of relevant experience, preferably with a mix of Big 4 audit and commercial accounting, less experience can be considered as a Senior Associate

  • QP candidate / CPA is a plus 

  • Proficiency in modern ERP systems (e.g. Oracle, NetSuite, or Expensify)

  • Experience with the Microsoft Office suite of programs is essential

  • Excellent written and spoken English

  • Good time management and an organized approach to tasks

  • Excellent attention to detail

  • Ability to take ownership and responsibility for assigned tasks

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team

  • A professional and positive attitude, remaining patient and calm under pressure

  • Willingness to learn and adapt in a fast-paced environment

  • Mandarin a plus; English essential.

Animoca Brands realizes its mission via three integrated business pillars: operating Web3 businesses to advance blockchain adoption with native projects such as Moca Network, Anichess, The Sandbox, Open Campus, NEOM Web3 initiatives, and a regulated stablecoin project in partnership with Standard Chartered and HKT; providing digital asset advisory services including tokenomics advisory, liquidity provisioning, and institutional research to help external Web3 projects grow; and investment management, with a portfolio of investments in over 540 companies including industry leaders Pudgy Penguins, Yuga Labs, Axie Infinity, Polygon, Consensys, Magic Eden, OpenSea, Dapper Labs, YGG, and many others.


Job Summary:
 
We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Executive Assistant to provide comprehensive support to our Executive Committee. As an Executive Assistant, you will be responsible for managing complex calendars, organizing meetings, and preparing high-quality presentations and decks. In addition to your administrative responsibilities, you will have the opportunity to immerse yourself in the Web3 landscape and expand your knowledge through exposure to our innovative projects and initiatives. This role requires exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and a passion for Web3 technologies.

Job Summary:
 
We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Executive Assistant to provide comprehensive support to our Executive Committee. As an Executive Assistant, you will be responsible for managing complex calendars, organizing meetings, and preparing high-quality presentations and decks. In addition to your administrative responsibilities, you will have the opportunity to immerse yourself in the Web3 landscape and expand your knowledge through exposure to our innovative projects and initiatives. This role requires exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and a passion for Web3 technologies.

lists.content:
• Manage and maintain the calendars of the Executive Committee, including scheduling meetings, appointments, and travel arrangements.
  • Coordinate and prioritize internal and external meetings, ensuring efficient use of executives' time and seamless coordination with stakeholders.
  • Prepare and distribute meeting agendas, minutes, and action items, following up on action items to ensure timely completion.
  • Assist in the preparation of high-quality presentations, decks, and reports for executive-level meetings
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather and consolidate input for presentations, ensuring accurate and up-to-date information.
  • Assist in the coordination and execution of special projects, events, and initiatives, working closely with the Executive Committee and other stakeholders.
  • Handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion and professionalism, maintaining the highest level of confidentiality at all times.
  • Act as a liaison between the Executive Committee and internal/external stakeholders, representing the executives in a professional and courteous manner.
  • Proactively identify opportunities for process improvements and implement streamlined approaches to enhance the efficiency of administrative operations.
  • Provide general administrative support, including managing email correspondence, personal matters, and handling other ad hoc tasks as assigned.

• Bachelor's degree in a relevant field or equivalent practical experience.
  • Proven experience as an Executive Assistant or in a similar role, supporting C-level executives or senior management.
  • Exceptional organizational and time management skills, with the ability to multitask and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accuracy while working on multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare and present information in a clear and concise manner.
  • Strong interest in Web3 technologies and a desire to expand knowledge in this field.
  • Self-motivated and proactive, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
  • Discretion and confidentiality when handling sensitive information.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines.
  • Proficiency in using productivity tools such as G Suite or Microsoft Office.

Job Summary:
 
We are seeking an AI Project Manager to lead the planning, execution, and delivery of innovative Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning initiatives. In this role, you will act as the critical bridge between our business stakeholders, data scientists, and engineering teams. You will be responsible for navigating the unique complexities of AI projects—from data collection and model training to deployment and performance monitoring — ensuring solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and drive real business value

lists.content:
• Lead the full lifecycle of AI project, including requirement gathering, feasibility assessment, data strategy, model development, testing, and production deployment.

  • Serve as the primary liaison between business teams and technical teams, translating complex business requirements into clear technical specifications and user stories.

  • Oversee specific AI phases such as data labeling, model training iterations, validation, and managing expectations around model accuracy and performance.

  • Identify potential project risks early and implement mitigation strategies.

  • Provide regular updates to leadership, clearly communicating technical bottlenecks, model metrics, and project progress in business-friendly terms.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field. Fresh graduates are also welcome to apply.

  • Previous internship experience in project management, tech operations, data analysis, or product management is a strong plus.

  • Proven track record of successfully delivering data science, machine learning, or AI projects to production.

  • Strong conceptual understanding of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing and Generative AI.

  • Understanding of data pipelines, data architecture, and the importance of data quality in model training.

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage the inherent uncertainties and experimental nature of AI projects.
