jobs.title: Senior Legal Counsel, Financial Partnerships & Regulatory
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Job Title: Senior Legal Counsel, Financial Partnerships & Regulatory
Department: Legal
Reports to: Head of Legal
Location: APAC


About Codex

Codex is building the infrastructure for stablecoin-based cross-border payments — moving money faster, cheaper, and more transparently than the legacy financial system. Backed by Circle, Coinbase, Dragonfly, Wintermute, and Cumberland, we're a small team solving hard problems at the intersection of crypto and global payments.


The Role
Codex's product offering and financial partnership network is expanding rapidly — new payment providers, banking partners, and liquidity providers globally. The legal work that underpins those relationships needs to move at the same pace as the business. This role exists to make that happen.

You'll own the legal workstream for financial partnerships end-to-end — reviewing and negotiating FP contracts, managing due diligence requests, and advising on the regulatory implications of new products, corridors, and partner structures. You'll work closely with the Head of Legal and report into the legal function, with tight day-to-day collaboration with the Financial Partnerships, Product and Compliance teams.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who has done this work before and can operate with a high degree of autonomy.

 

Responsibilities

Financial Partnership Contracts

  • Review, negotiate, and execute commercial agreements with financial partners — payment providers, banking counterparties, liquidity providers, and PSPs

  • Own the contract lifecycle end-to-end: preparing markups, tracking open issues, coordinating with counterparties, and driving to execution without losing momentum

  • Maintain and update standard form FP agreements as the regulatory and commercial environment evolves

  • Advise the Financial Partnerships and Sales teams on commercial terms, entity routing, and deal structuring across multi-entity, multi-jurisdiction arrangements

Financial Partner RFIs & Due Diligence

  • Manage inbound legal and regulatory due diligence requests from financial partners — collating documentation, preparing regulatory status summaries, and coordinating with Compliance on AML/CFT-related queries

  • Prepare and maintain legal memos, licensing summaries, and corporate documentation packages for partners requiring clarity on Codex's regulatory status and entity structure

  • Ensure Codex's outbound KYB documentation to financial partners is accurate, current, and responsive

Product Regulatory Analysis

  • Analyse the regulatory implications of new products, payment corridors, and client segments before they go live — identifying licensing requirements, restrictions, and structural considerations across relevant jurisdictions

  • Advise Product and Engineering on the legal constraints that affect feature design, entity routing, and market entry sequencing

  • Monitor regulatory developments across key jurisdictions (APAC, LATAM, EMEA) and brief the legal and business teams on material changes


What We're Looking For

  • Qualified lawyer with 10+ years of experience, ideally combining a first-tier law firm foundation with in-house experience at a fintech payments company

  • Deep expertise in financial partnership contracts and payments regulation — this is a domain specialist role, not a generalist one

  • Comfortable operating autonomously: you can pick up a complex contract, identify the issues, and drive it to execution without needing significant direction

  • Commercially aware — you understand that legal is an enabler of the business, not a gate, and you give advice accordingly

  • Meticulous and detail-oriented, with the communication skills to translate complex legal positions into clear guidance for non-lawyers

  • Based in APAC or a time zone that overlaps meaningfully with the team


Nice to Have

  • Experience across multiple APAC and other regions and familiarity with the regulatory frameworks governing cross-border payments and digital assets in the region

  • Exposure to stablecoin or digital asset regulation

  • Prior experience as a solo or early legal hire at a fast-growing fintech

jobs.title: Go-To-Market (GTM) Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Job Title: GTM Engineer
Department: Marketing & Growth
Reports to: Marketing Lead & Sales Lead
Location: Flexible / Remote

About Codex

Codex is building the infrastructure for stablecoin-based cross-border payments — moving money faster, cheaper, and more transparently than the legacy financial system. Backed by Circle, Coinbase, Dragonfly, Wintermute, and Cumberland, we're a small team solving hard problems at the intersection of crypto and global payments.


The Role
Codex is growing fast — new clients, new markets, new financial partners. The pipeline that feeds that growth runs on outbound, and outbound needs a dedicated owner.


As GTM Engineer, you'll build and scale the systems that get Codex in front of the right buyers: PSPs, remittance companies, fintechs, and institutional clients across globally. That means owning the full stack — sending infrastructure, lead sourcing and enrichment, ICP scoring, campaign operations — and delivering qualified meetings to a growing regional sales team.


This is a hands-on builder role that is performance and metrics-driven. You'll inherit a functioning outbound engine and your job is to scale it, sharpen it, and expand it. You’ll start off with being a heads-down operator: running campaigns, maintaining deliverability, iterating on sequences, and making sure what you're sending is converting. As volume grows, the role expands into broader demand generation ownership — new channels, ABM plays, and beyond.


You'll work closely with both the Marketing Lead and Sales Lead, and be a key part of how Codex scales its commercial reach across every region it operates in.

 

Responsibilities

Outbound Infrastructure & Deliverability

  • Own the sending infrastructure end-to-end — domain and mailbox management, warmup, deliverability monitoring, and inbox placement across email and LinkedIn campaigns at scale

  • Maintain and evolve the enrichment and orchestration stack: data sourcing, waterfall enrichment, ICP scoring, and routing logic

  • Own the sequencer and multi-channel outreach stack (email, LinkedIn, and more) — campaign setup, A/B testing, reply handling, and ongoing optimisation

  • Ensure no rep or outreach domain/account is double-contacted; build the deduplication and routing logic that keeps the system clean

Lead Generation & Enrichment Pipelines

  • Build and run automated pipelines for lead sourcing, enrichment, and ICP qualification — using AI/LLM workflows, APIs, and automation platforms

  • Develop signal- and intent-based prospecting workflows that surface high-fit accounts before they're being worked by competitors

  • Research and maintain ICP definitions for each regional market

  • Build personalisation at scale: automated company research, dynamic copy generation, and multi-variable sequence logic

Pipeline Delivery & Sales Alignment

  • Own the CRM as the operational backbone of the sales and marketing function — maintaining data integrity, pipeline structure, lifecycle stages, and campaign attribution across the full funnel

  • Own the qualified meeting target: track volumes, reply rates, meeting bookings, and pipeline attribution, and report on what's working and what isn't

  • Build and maintain the lead routing and handoff logic between outbound systems and the regional sales reps — ensuring warm leads are passed cleanly with full context

  • Create feedback loops with the sales team: what's converting, what's not, which ICPs are responding, and where copy or targeting needs to change

  • Support reactivation campaigns for dormant accounts and inbound leads that haven't converted

Systems & Automation

  • Own the integration layer between outbound platforms and our CRM — data hygiene, attribution, and campaign reporting

  • Build automation workflows that reduce manual work across the marketing and sales function without sacrificing quality or personalisation

  • Stay current on the GTM tooling landscape and proactively propose and test new tools, signals, and approaches

 

What We're Looking For

  • 3 to 5 years of hands-on GTM engineering, growth, or outbound experience at a B2B fintech, payments company, or SaaS business — or as a GTM engineer at an outbound agency running campaigns across multiple B2B clients

  • Built or meaningfully scaled an outbound motion with pipeline numbers you can defend: sending volumes, reply rates, meetings booked, pipeline influenced

  • Daily hands-on with modern GTM stack: Enrichment/orchestration, email sequencers, LinkedIn automation, CRM, and deliverability at scale

  • Strong automation and integration skills — you build the plumbing, not just the campaigns

  • AI-native in how you work — LLMs and automation are your default operating mode, not a line on your CV

  • Startup or agency background where you were the builder, not one seat in a large organisation

Nice to Have

  • Background in fintech, payments, stablecoins, or crypto — ideally with outbound aimed at PSPs, remittance companies, neobanks, or institutional buyers

  • Experience with signal- or intent-based prospecting workflows

  • Familiarity with the cross-border payments ecosystem and the buying behaviour of the clients Codex sells to

Job Title: Senior Product Manager
Department: Product Management
Reports to: Co-Founder (Product)
Location: Remote

About Codex

Codex is building the infrastructure for stablecoin-based cross-border payments — moving money faster, cheaper, and more transparently than the legacy financial system. Backed by Circle, Coinbase, Dragonfly, Wintermute, and Cumberland, we're a small team solving hard problems at the intersection of crypto and global payments.

The Role

As Senior Product Manager, you'll own 3P payouts and collections end-to-end — from how money flows in via virtual accounts and collections rails, to how it flows out via FP integrations and direct banking rails. You'll be the payments expert in the room: the person who knows which FPs are worth integrating, how to design a user journey for our clients, and how to specify something that an engineer can actually build.

What we need is someone who is deeply payments-native and can operate as the domain owner from day one.

 

Responsibilities

Product Ownership — Payouts & Collections

  • Own the 3P payout and collections product end-to-end — from strategy and prioritisation through to spec, build, and launch

  • Define and maintain the product roadmap for FP integrations and direct banking rail integrations as the business scales

  • Write detailed, buildable specs — engineers should be able to ship from what you produce

  • Design the user journey and frontend experience for payout and collections flows, with strong opinions about what a client actually needs to see and do

Financial Partner Strategy & Integration

  • Evaluate FPs and banking partners across pricing, rail coverage, onboarding complexity, licensing constraints, and operational reliability — and make clear recommendations on which to integrate and in what sequence

  • Lead the integration process with new FPs end-to-end: scoping, spec, coordination with Engineering, and go-live

  • Understand the FOF implications of each FP and banking relationship, and design around the constraints rather than discovering them after the fact

  • Stay current on the FP and payments infrastructure market — who the relevant players are, what they're good at, and where the gotchas are

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Work day-to-day with the co-founders, Customer Operations, and the Engineering team

  • Align with Financial Partnerships on which FPs and banks are being evaluated, and feed product requirements into the partnership prioritisation process

  • Work closely with Compliance and Legal on licensing constraints and fund safeguarding requirements

  • Surface client feedback on payout and collections UX to inform the roadmap — you'll be talking to clients directly


What We're Looking For

  • 6 to 10 years of product experience, with meaningful depth in cross-border payments infrastructure — payouts, collections, virtual accounts, and FP/banking integrations

  • Must have shipped both directions of money movement: outbound payouts and inbound collections

  • Prior hands-on integration experience with payment infrastructure providers Payments-native: you understand flow of funds, rail mechanics, corridor-specific constraints, and how licensing affects what you can build

  • Opinionated about UX for a B2B payments ICP — you know what a client needs to see when they place an order, and you can design for it

  • Background at a licensed cross-border payments company or stablecoin payments shop at Series A–C scale

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Job Title: Software Engineer
Department: Engineering & Product Development
Reports to: Engineering Lead
Location: Flexible but Singapore preferred

About Codex
Codex is building the infrastructure for stablecoin-based cross-border payments — moving money faster, cheaper, and more transparently than the legacy financial system. Backed by Circle, Coinbase, Dragonfly, Wintermute, and Cumberland, we're a small team solving hard problems at the intersection of crypto and global payments.

 

The Role
You'll own Codex's financial partner integrations end-to-end — from API contract and webhook design through to reconciliation and production hardening — and build the automation layer that makes our trading and treasury operations increasingly self-running.

This is a high-ownership role at the infrastructure layer of the business. You'll be adding new payment rails, eliminating manual operational workflows, and designing systems that handle real money reliably across fiat and crypto rails. You'll work directly with the founders and Engineering & Product Development team, and closely with Compliance, Operations, and Financial Partnerships.

 

Responsibilities

Financial Partner Integrations

  • Own integrations with banks, payment providers, and liquidity venues end-to-end — from API contract and webhook design through to production hardening and reconciliation

  • Build integrations that are robust to vendor reality: incomplete documentation, schema changes without warning, and validation rules that shift post-go-live

  • Build messaging / notification systems with signature verification and replay protection; pin schemas against real sandbox behaviour; design for failure at every layer

  • Maintain and evolve the reconciliation layer across all connected payment rails — fees, settlement windows, and exception handling as first-class concerns

Operational Automation

  • Identify manual workflows in onboarding, compliance, and back-office operations and systematically replace them with product and automation

  • Enable self-service for internal ops teams and customers, reducing engineering dependency for routine operational tasks

  • Work closely with Compliance and Operations to understand where the friction is and build the tooling that removes it

Treasury & Liquidity Automation

  • Design and build the automation layer for Codex's trading and treasury operations — automated position management, liquidity routing, and risk controls

  • Design for failure: clear handling of automated decision failures, position unwinding, and safe degradation

Engineering Standards

  • Set and maintain the engineering standard for how payment integrations are built at Codex — idempotency, audit trails, fail-closed design, exact decimal arithmetic, and deterministic durable orchestration

  • Mentor engineers on the hard parts of money movement systems

  • Continuously design and build for security, hardening our systems

  • Ship and critically review AI-assisted code with the judgement to identify plausible but incorrect output or output detrimental to a product’s long-term health and sustainability


What We're Looking For

  • 6 to 10 years of backend engineering experience in cross-border payments, stablecoins, FX infrastructure, or crypto custody

  • Production experience with both crypto rails (on-chain settlement on major networks like Ethereum, Tron and Solana; bridging major stablecoins; DeFi protocols) and fiat rails (SWIFT, SEPA, local schemes such as FPS or CHATS)

  • Must-have: Production experience with durable workflow orchestration — Temporal strongly preferred. Includes deterministic replay, safe versioning of live workflows, idempotency keys, and compensation logic

  • Must-have: Strong TypeScript/Node and Postgres in a money context — fail-closed design, exact decimal arithmetic, append-only audit trails

  • Must-have: Hands-on third-party API integration experience, including vendors with incomplete documentation, webhook reliability requirements, and schema instability

jobs.title: SVP of Supply Chain Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Cambium is a modern American wood manufacturer, distributor, and technology company connecting and modernizing the wood economy. We work with architects, builders, and leading brands across the built environment, including Amazon, Room & Board, and Equinox. Our work has been recognized by Time's Best Inventions and Fast Company's Innovation by Design Awards. Technology is how we match supply to demand across a fragmented industry.

The American hardwood industry has lost more than half its sawmills in the last two decades. Quality trees go to waste, and the US imports more lumber than it produces, even though domestic capacity could meet nearly all of our needs. Until now, this industry forced a choice: local relationships or national scale, meaningful materials or modern efficiency. We don't think those are real tradeoffs. We're building the infrastructure to prove it, with modern software, better supply chains, and a clear view of what comes next: a wood economy that's local, efficient, and built to last.

About This Role

As Cambium’s SVP of Supply Chain, you’ll take the leading role in developing and expanding Cambium’s supply chains across our 3 go-to-market segments: millwork, mass timber, and furniture. You’ll oversee a national supplier, production, and distribution network that includes both vertically integrated hubs and a rapidly expanding ecosystem of third-party partners. You’ll bridge the gap between high-level strategy and on-the-ground execution, creating the critical infrastructure needed to enable historic volume growth. This is a role for a battle-tested operator who embodies Extreme Ownership and thrives at the intersection of people and process management.

What You’ll Do Here

  • Design & Execute Fulfillment Strategy: oversee the fulfillment of Cambium’s wood offerings – across the company’s national network of supply partners within select vertically integrated manufacturing/distribution hubs.

  • Strategic Leadership: work cross-functionally to inform physical product strategy – including SKU architecture, pricing models, product development, and market entry strategies.

  • Ensure Operational Excellence: Work across Cambium’s internal sites to establish and enforce rigorous quality control and assurance protocols, standardize production efficiencies, and streamline staffing management.

  • Logistics & Distribution Management: oversee national transportation strategy and warehouse operations, optimizing for both speed and cost-to-serve.

  • Implement Processes to Enable Growth: manage systems architecture to increase supply chain efficiency while scaling volumes. Own and improve upon core fulfillment metrics (including capacity, throughput rates, COGs, etc).

Your Skill Sets and Capabilities Include

  • Proven Scale-Up Experience: 12+ years of leadership in supply chain or operations management, with experience in high-growth scaling. Specific manufacturing and/or distribution experience within the wood products or building materials industry preferred.

  • Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence: you’re able to translate complex operational constraints into clear strategic narratives for the CEO, Board, and Sales leadership to inform business decisions.

  • Management Expertise: you’ve overseen high-performing fulfillment teams across multiple geographic sites – both externally facilitated and vertically integrated. You embody Cambium’s “extreme ownership” and “people first” core values in your management approach.

  • Operational & Financial Rigor: you have a proven ability to design and optimize manufacturing and distribution systems, leveraging data to drive performance improvements. You’re capable of implementing real-time dashboards to drive accountability across production teams – specific experience with NetSuite preferred.

  • Quality at Scale: You’re well versed in establishing QA/QC protocols (e.g., Six Sigma, Lean Manufacturing, or ISO standards) that significantly reduced failure rates, waste, and "re-work" costs. Preference for specific experience with wood, lumber, or forest products supply chains..

The Details

  • This role will report to: Marisa Repka, COO

  • Salary Range: $210,000 - $260,000 total compensation, commensurate with experience

  • When: We're looking to fill this role immediately

  • Where: Baltimore, MD; Washington, D.C, or Duluth, MN (highly preferred). Significant travel required.

Benefits and Perks

  • Equity options package

  • Flexible PTO and schedule

  • 401k with employer matching

  • Comprehensive medical, dental & vision insurance

  • Work with an incredibly smart, diverse, mission-driven team

  • An opportunity to play a core role in defining our fast-growing company

  • Volunteer tree planting days

Cambium is committed to building an inclusive organization that reflects the diverse communities our team works to serve. We believe that diversity in all its forms (gender, race, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion, veteran's status, disability and more) is essential to imagining and actively building a more just and sustainable future for all. We hope you feel welcome here. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.title: VP of Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Cambium is the AI-powered platform modernizing the wood economy, and we're looking for a seasoned engineering leader whose business instincts are as sharp as their technical depth. As VP of Engineering, you'll own the engineering organization behind a data heavy product that helps wood buyers and suppliers make better decisions and build better physical products — the team, the delivery systems, and the standards it's held to. Some of our digital platform is in production; much of it is still 0→1, and you're the kind of leader who moves without waiting for all the answers.

You'll partner closely with the CEO and the Senior Director of Product. Product owns the what and the why; you own how the organization delivers: people, process, and budget. You'll have the latitude to shape the team to fit where the platform is headed rather than inherit it as-is. This is a role for a decisive leader who'll roll up their sleeves early, bring the discipline to scale, and earn trust through action.

What You'll Do Here

  • Champion engineering across the company: bridge business needs and engineering reality with non-technical stakeholders — clearly, directly, without ego.

  • Partner directly with the Senior Director of Product and CEO to align technical execution with product strategy and ensure Cambium's technology improves user experience, data transparency, and operational functionality.

  • Build, mentor, and scale the engineering team: hiring, career ladders, performance, and retention. Culture, craft, and ownership are non-negotiable.

  • Put in place the processes, team structure, and capacity planning that let a growing team ship predictably.

  • Own the engineering budget and technology strategy, including build-vs-buy decisions, vendor selection, and how AI tooling factors into headcount and team design.

  • Own the data strategy across business systems of record like NetSuite and Hubspot (owned by other depts) and our custom platform (owned by engineering): set the standards for how they exchange data and which one is the source of truth.

  • Apply AI/ML tooling with intention — enhancing platform capabilities without losing focus on resilience and scalability.

Your Skill Sets and Capabilities Include

  • 15+ years leading engineering teams at scale; Series B or growth-stage experience required. A track record of hiring, mentoring, and building cultures of ownership.

  • Deep technical foundation: you've designed and shipped complex systems in domains like logistics, fintech, and customer-facing platforms, and can still stress-test an architecture, challenge assumptions, and make a build-vs-buy call. You measure your impact by what the organization ships, not by your own output.

  • Familiar with the challenges of keeping data consistent across multiple databases — sync issues, conflicting sources of truth, schema drift — and has worked through both technical and organizational solutions to address those challenges.

  • Proven ability to move through ambiguity without losing momentum or dropping projects.

  • Strong backbone: you give and receive direct feedback, push back with conviction, and build trust through honesty. You collaborate closely with other teams, translating complex business requirements into practical technical solutions.

  • Actively evaluates and stress-tests AI/ML tooling for real workflow integration — not just awareness, but hands-on judgment about what ships and what doesn't, including how it factors into headcount and team structure decisions.

  • Bachelor's in CS or Engineering; master's preferred.

The Details

  • This role will report to: Ben Christensen, CEO

  • Salary Range: $250,000 - $320,000 plus bonus

  • When: We’re looking to fill this role immediately

  • Where: San Francisco, CA hybrid 3x/week

Benefits and Perks

  • Equity options package

  • Unlimited PTO and flexible schedule

  • 401k matching

  • Comprehensive medical, dental & vision insurance

  • Work with an incredibly smart, diverse, climate mission-driven team

  • An opportunity to play a core role in defining our fast-growing company

  • Volunteer tree planting days

Cambium is committed to building an inclusive organization that reflects the diverse communities our team works to serve. We believe that diversity in all its forms (gender, race, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion, veteran's status, disability and more) is essential to imagining and actively building a more just and sustainable future for all. We hope you feel welcome here. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.title: (Lumber) Shop Hand
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About This Role

As Shop Hand, you’ll be a key part of daily operations at our East Coast manufacturing facility. This role requires confidence working with woodshop tools and millwork equipment, attention to detail, and a strong commitment to safety, speed, and consistency. You’ll be hands-on across every step of the production process. From drying and milling final fabrication, you’ll be part of a tight-knit team focused on delivering high-quality, Carbon Smart Wood™ products.

What You’ll Do Here

  • Assist the Sr. Shop Manager in fulfilling orders and keeping the shop organized and running smoothly

  • Operate shop equipment to process raw boards into finished products, including cutting, planing, sanding, and assembly

  • Load and unload materials, move inventory, and stage materials for production

  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment by following shop protocols and daily cleanup routines Sr Shop Manager to effectively fulfill orders and maintain a clean working environment.

  • Support packaging, labeling, and shipping of finished goods as needed

Your Skill Sets and Capabilities Include

  • You’re comfortable with power tools and woodshop machinery

  • You work safely and stay alert in a factory or woodshop environment

  • You hustle—staying focused, moving with purpose, and taking pride in hard work

  • You proactively create value, reliable and bring attention to detail

  • You take feedback well and actively seek to improve your skills

  • You’re a team player who supports others and leaves your ego at the door

  • Must be able to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly throughout the shift, including handling lumber

  • Frequent standing, walking, bending, reaching, and handling of materials and tools.

  • Comfortable working in a warehouse or millwork shop environment with fluctuating temperatures, sawdust, and noise.

The Details

  • This role will report to: Michael Sheets, Sr Shop Manager

  • Salary Range: $20.00/Hour

  • Interview Process: Recruiter screen, Hiring Manager Interview, Final On-Site Interview

From drying and milling final fabrication, you’ll be part of a tight-knit team focused on delivering high-quality, Carbon Smart Wood™ products.


What You’ll Do Here

 - Assist the Sr. Shop Manager in fulfilling orders and keeping the shop organized and running smoothly

 - Operate shop equipment to process raw boards into finished products, including cutting, planing, sanding, and assembly

 - Load and unload materials, move inventory, and stage materials for production

 - Maintain a clean and safe work environment by following shop protocols and daily cleanup routines Sr Shop Manager to effectively fulfill orders and maintain a clean working environment.

 - Support packaging, labeling, and shipping of finished goods as needed
   
   

Your Skill Sets and Capabilities Include

 - You’re comfortable with power tools and woodshop machinery

 - You work safely and stay alert in a factory or woodshop environment

 - You hustle—staying focused, moving with purpose, and taking pride in hard work

 - You proactively create value, reliable and bring attention to detail

 - You take feedback well and actively seek to improve your skills

 - You’re a team player who supports others and leaves your ego at the door

 - Must be able to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly throughout the shift, including handling lumber

 - Frequent standing, walking, bending, reaching, and handling of materials and tools.

 - Comfortable working in a warehouse or millwork shop environment with fluctuating temperatures, sawdust, and noise.
   

The Details

 - This role will report to: Michael Sheets, Sr Shop Manager

 - Salary Range: $20.00/Hour

 - When: Immediately

 - Where: Columbia, MD

 - Interview Process: Recruiter screen, Hiring Manager Interview, Final On-Site Interview

jobs.title: Director of Lifecycle + Growth Marketing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Who We Are

Cambium is a modern American wood manufacturer, distributor, and technology company connecting and modernizing the wood economy. We work with architects, builders, and leading brands across the built environment, including Amazon, Room & Board, and Equinox.

Our work has been recognized by Time's Best Inventions and Fast Company's Innovation by Design Awards. Technology is how we match supply to demand across a fragmented industry.

The American hardwood industry has lost more than half its sawmills in the last two decades. Quality trees go to waste, and the US imports more lumber than it produces, even though domestic capacity could meet nearly all of our needs. Until now, this industry forced a choice: local relationships or national scale, meaningful materials or modern efficiency. We don't think those are real tradeoffs. We're building the infrastructure to prove it, with modern software, better supply chains, and a clear view of what comes next: a wood economy that's local, efficient, and built to last.

Role Overview

An architect specs our material on one project, a builder installs it, and every one of them has a next project. The gap between the first order and the second, and between the one product a customer knows us for and the full range we supply, is our biggest lever. Nobody owns it today.

You'll own lifecycle for Cambium end to end, reporting to the VP Marketing and working closely with Sales and Supply. Some quarters the most interesting problem won't look like lifecycle at all. If that sounds like the fun part, this is your role.

Who You Are

  • A generalist: Range and judgment. You've built across the marketing stack, and you can tell the difference between the problem that's loud and the one that's important.

  • You have taste: In a world where anyone can generate anything, you pride yourself on curation: knowing what's worth sending, what's worth building, and what a customer will actually notice.

  • Technology is your default: When you hit a problem, your first move is to find a creative way to solve it with tools, whether that's an automation, an enrichment workflow, or something you stitch together yourself. You see it, you take action, you figure it out, and you're excited by that.

  • A systems thinker: You see the customer relationship as one connected system, from first inquiry to fifth project, and you build the infrastructure that holds it together.

  • High ownership, high slope: You ask questions before you answer, you're comfortable being handed a problem with no clear owner, and when more customers come back for a second project, you want it to be because of something you built.

What You'll Do

  • Own lifecycle for Cambium: you build the strategy and ultimately own the results, including retention, expansion, and how customers move across our product range and our brands.

  • Partner with Sales and Supply on the customer experience: Build the programs, pressure-test them in live accounts, and change them the moment a customer tells you they're wrong.

  • Define and run our customer marketing playbook for acquisitions: M&A is a big part of how Cambium grows, and every company we buy comes with its own customers. You own how they're brought into Cambium and what they hear from us, and you run the playbook for the next deal.

  • Scale from the 10k foot view down to the minutiae: what share of customers come back within a year, and what's the number we plan against? Why did this account go quiet in March? Why is this HubSpot workflow firing twice, and what's the fix?

What You'll Need

  • 10+ years in marketing at high-growth startups, with real ownership of retention, lifecycle, or growth somewhere in that time.

  • Something you can point to that didn't exist before you: a function, a program, a system, built from close to nothing, as a team lead or a senior IC.

  • Experience at a high-growth startup, where you built things before there was a process for them.

  • Deep proficiency in HubSpot or an equivalent customer engagement tool (Braze, Iterable, Klaviyo) and hands-on with AI and automation tools. You build it yourself.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in physical products, construction, or building materials, or any industry where the buyer is a professional with a project.

  • Experience integrating an acquired company's customers or CRM.

  • Early-stage experience where you built the lifecycle stack rather than inheriting one.

The Details

  • This role will report to: VP Marketing

  • Salary Range: $160-190K

  • When: November 1st 2026

  • Where: San Francisco, 3x/week in our beautiful office in the Presidio!

Benefits and Perks

  • Equity options package

  • Flexible PTO

  • 401k matching

  • Comprehensive medical, dental & vision insurance

  • Work with an incredibly smart, diverse, climate mission-driven team

  • An opportunity to play a core role in defining our fast-growing company

  • Volunteer tree planting days

Cambium is committed to building an inclusive organization that reflects the diverse communities our team works to serve. We believe that diversity in all its forms (gender, race, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion, veteran's status, disability and more) is essential to imagining and actively building a more just and sustainable future for all. We hope you feel welcome here. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.title: Senior Accounting Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Cambium is a growth stage start-up using technology to make it easy to access material we normally waste, turning salvaged lumber into Carbon Smart Wood™. We recently closed a $18.5M Series A funding round to make it easier to buy, sell, and move fiber across the supply chain. In addition to being named one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies of 2024, we serve clients like Amazon, Equinox, Room & Board, and other leading brands in the construction, design, and furniture industries. It’s an exciting time of growth for Cambium, and we’re looking for ambitious, energetic people to join our mission.

About This Role

We are seeking a highly skilled Accountant to join our growing finance team. This role is central to ensuring the accuracy, compliance, and integrity of our financial operations as we scale. You will own core accounting processes in NetSuite, manage monthly closes, and strengthen reporting controls across the parent company and subsidiaries.

This is a hands-on position for someone with proven NetSuite expertise, CPA credentials, and experience in manufacturing and inventory environments. You will work closely with our Finance Operations Manager to ensure precision in our books, compliance with accounting standards, and scalable processes to support rapid growth.

What You’ll Do Here

  • Lead the month-end close process across the parent company and two small subsidiaries, completing within ten business days.

  • Ensure accurate reconciliations in NetSuite, including COGS, debt schedules, asset tracking, AP/AR, and other balance sheet items.

  • Clean up and validate historical transactions, including migrating and updating data from legacy ERPs (QuickBooks, Sage).

  • Manage external accounting contractors to complete accounting and reporting requirements from management.

  • Oversee ERP integrity, ensuring NetSuite reflects accurate, real-time data.

  • Support external audit processes and maintain compliance with accounting standards.

  • Provide granular reporting on key metrics such as margins, time to payment, and deal data segmented by region, product family, channel, and deal type.

  • Partner with the Finance Operations Manager to ensure accurate project costing, and vendor/client communications.

  • Maintain oversight of inventory and work in process accuracy.

Qualifications (Must-Haves)

  • 6-10 years of related accounting experience.

  • Certified Public Accountant at some point prior.

  • Hands-on NetSuite accounting and reconciliation experience across parent and subsidiaries.

  • Strong background in manufacturing and inventory accounting.

  • QuickBooks experience.

  • Proven ability to lead month-end close processes independently.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience participating in or leading a financial audit.

  • Prior experience in high-growth or acquisition-heavy environments.

  • Familiarity with migrating financial data from multiple ERPs.

The Details

  • This role will report to: VP of Finance

  • Salary Range: $140-195k

  • When: We’re looking to fill this role immediately

  • Where: SF 3x/week ideal, open to fully remote candidates outside of the Bay Area

Benefits and Perks

  • Equity options package

  • Unlimited PTO and flexible schedule

  • 401k matching

  • Comprehensive medical, dental & vision insurance

  • Work with an incredibly smart, diverse, climate mission-driven team

  • An opportunity to play a core role in defining our fast-growing company

  • Volunteer tree planting days

Data Analyst Intern (Finance) - January to May 2027
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Role

We're looking for a Data Analyst Intern to work with our data team on the numbers Finance relies on.

Every financial report, reconciliation and month-end figure at Coinhako depends on data being right. You'll work on the analysis and checks behind those numbers — reconciling figures against independent sources, investigating why two reports disagree, and turning checks that someone currently does by hand into something that runs on its own.

This is real work on production data, scoped so you can finish things. You'll be given problems with a clear question and a clear finish line, and you'll have someone to ask when you get stuck.

A number being "right" is not always obvious. No single source is definitive — venues disagree, references lag, and a figure that looks wrong is often just the market moving. You'll learn how we decide what to trust, and why "I'm not sure yet, here's what I checked" is a better answer than a confident wrong one.

Day to day, your work answers questions like: Do these two reports agree, and if not, why? Which figure is the right one to use? Can this check be automated so nobody has to remember to run it?

What You’ll Do

Check that our numbers are correct

  • Reconcile financial figures against independent sources and explain any differences you find

  • Investigate when a report looks wrong, and work out whether it actually is

  • Trace a number back to where it came from

Automate the manual checks

  • Take a check someone currently runs by hand each week and turn it into something scheduled and reliable

  • Write SQL and Python to pull, compare and validate financial data

  • Make missing data visible rather than silent

Make the reporting easier to use

  • Build and maintain dashboards Finance uses to monitor financial performance

  • Document what a dataset means and what it excludes, so the next person doesn't have to ask

What We’re Looking For

  • No professional experience needed. We care about how you think and how carefully you work.

  • Currently studying, or recently graduated, in a numerate field — data, statistics, finance, accounting, computer science, engineering or similar

  • SQL — you've written queries with joins and aggregations, and you can read someone else's

  • Some Python, for analysis or automation

  • You're careful with numbers. You check your own output before you show it to anyone, and you notice when a total doesn't add up

  • You're comfortable saying "I don't know." We would much rather hear that than a confident answer that turns out to be wrong

  • You ask why a number is what it is, not just what it is

  • Clear written communication — a lot of this job is explaining a discrepancy to someone who isn't technical

What You'll Learn

  • How financial reporting and reconciliation actually work in a live crypto business

  • How to decide which number is the right number when several sources disagree

  • Building and running automated data checks and pipelines

  • Working with production data properly — version control, review, and not breaking things

  • Using AI tooling well: we provide it, and we'll show you how we use it here

Nice To Have

  • Coursework or personal projects involving financial, accounting or transaction data

  • Any experience with dashboards — Power BI, QuickSight, Tableau, or similar

  • Exposure to spreadsheets at scale, and an understanding of where they stop being safe

  • Interest in crypto or trading

What’s in it for you

  • Friendly and fun start-up work culture

  • Convenient work location located in the heart of CBD area

  • Vibrant office with a well-stocked pantry

Find out more about Coinhako here https://www.coinhako.com/ and don't forget to visit our Careers Page https://www.coinhako.com/join-us

By submitting your application to us, you consent to the collection, use, disclosure and processing of your personal data in accordance with our privacy policy, which is accessible at https://www.coinhako.com/legal/sg-1/privacy_policy.

jobs.title: Crypto Options Trader
jobs.descriptionHtml:
What you'll be doing:

  • Contribute to a trading book and generate revenues and manage risk for the respective business

  • Pricing & Volatility: Implement volatility models and maintain real-time volatility surfaces for crypto assets like Bitcoin and Ethereum. Principal market maker for the various crypto assets.

  • Risk Management: Monitor and manage the trading book's risk, ensuring Delta, Gamma, Vega, Theta, and Rho exposures are within strict limits.

  • Strategy Execution: Develop and refine systematic strategies to identify short-term mispricing and execute market-making operations.

  • Research & Development: Partner with developers to backtest, prototype, and deploy new options strategies. Develop new products for distribution

  • Post-Trade Analysis: Perform deep-dive P&L and Greek exposure analysis to evaluate performance and optimize trading models.

  • Work in close partnership with control functions such as Legal, Compliance, Risk, and Finance in order to ensure appropriate governance and control infrastructure

What we're looking for:

  • Education: Degree in Financial Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, or Economics from a top-tier institution.

  • Experience: Typically 3+ years of hands-on experience in options trading (equities, FX, or crypto) and algorithmic market making.

  • Technical Skills: Strong programming capabilities, particularly in Python

  • Market Knowledge: In-depth understanding of FX, equity and crypto market mechanics (CeFi, DeFi, perpetual futures, and margin models).

 

What’s in it for you:

  • Friendly and fun start-up work culture

  • Convenient work location located in the heart of CBD area

  • Generous annual leaves on top of national holidays

  • Medical coverage including GP, Specialist, TCM, and more

  • Self-care benefits and exciting fitness workshops/webinars

  • Vibrant office with a well-stocked pantry

 

Find out more about Coinhako here https://www.coinhako.com/ and don't forget to visit our Careers Page https://www.coinhako.com/join-us

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The Head of Engineering will be responsible for leading the product engineering strategy and execution for the organization. This individual will work closely with the executive team, product managers, and other stakeholders to ensure that all product engineering efforts align with business objectives, market needs, and technical excellence.

You will build, manage, and mentor a high-performing engineering team, providing leadership across various product development initiatives. As a hands-on leader, you will oversee the entire product development lifecycle, from ideation to deployment, ensuring the delivery of robust, secure, and user-friendly crypto solutions.

What you'll be doing:

  • Strategic Leadership:

    • Define and execute the technical vision and strategy for the platform, ensuring alignment with the company’s goals.

    • Lead the engineering team to build scalable, secure, and high-performance features for the exchange, with a focus on availability, security, and usability.

    • Collaborate with executive leadership and product managers to create and refine the engineering roadmap, prioritizing key initiatives to drive business growth.

  • Team Leadership and Development:

    • Manage, mentor, and inspire a team of product engineers, fostering a culture of technical excellence, innovation, and accountability.

    • Recruit top talent, develop engineering leadership within the team, and establish career development frameworks to grow internal talent.

    • Encourage cross-functional collaboration and ensure effective communication between engineering, product, UX/UI, security, and operations teams.

  • Product Development and Delivery:

    • Oversee the end-to-end product engineering lifecycle, from ideation to implementation, ensuring features are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest quality standards.

    • Provide leadership in the architecture and design of scalable, low-latency systems, ensuring high throughput for trading operations.

    • Drive continuous product improvements, responding quickly to market changes and customer feedback, while ensuring regulatory compliance and security standards.

  • Platform Scalability and Performance:

    • Ensure the platform is optimized for scalability, with the ability to handle high volumes of transactions, low latency, and seamless performance during peak periods.

    • Champion best practices in software engineering, including automated testing, continuous integration, and monitoring.

    • Manage and improve the platform’s infrastructure, focusing on high availability, redundancy, and disaster recovery processes.

  • Security and Compliance:

    • Ensure that platform security is a top priority, implementing best practices and industry standards for data protection, anti-money laundering (AML), and know your customer (KYC) compliance.

    • Lead initiatives to continuously evaluate and enhance the platform’s security posture, proactively identifying and mitigating risks.

    • Work with the legal and compliance teams to ensure that product development and engineering are aligned with regulatory requirements.

  • Innovation and Market Leadership:

    • Stay at the forefront of emerging trends in fintech, blockchain, and digital asset exchanges, driving the adoption of new technologies and practices to improve the platform.

    • Conduct research and development on innovative solutions to enhance the exchange’s capabilities, such as enhanced trading algorithms, risk management tools, and blockchain integrations.

  • Process Improvement and Efficiency:

    • Establish and refine engineering processes to enhance efficiency, transparency, and collaboration across teams.

    • Implement metrics and performance KPIs to measure the success of engineering initiatives and the overall product engineering function.

What we're looking for:

  • Experience:

    • Minimum of 10+ years of experience in product engineering roles, with at least 5+ years in a leadership capacity managing engineering teams.

    • Proven track record of leading the development of broker-dealer trading systems platforms or similar complex financial systems (e.g., quantitative trading systems, order book, risk management systems).

    • Strong understanding of cryptocurrency and digital asset markets, trading systems, and exchange architectures is a significant advantage.

    • Experience in building highly available, low-latency, and high-performance financial applications.

  • Technical Skills:

    • Expertise in software architecture and engineering best practices (microservices, APIs, distributed systems).

    • Hands-on experience with modern programming languages (e.g., Ruby, Python, Go, Java, C++) and relevant tech stacks.

    • In-depth knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) and containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).

    • Familiarity with blockchain technology, smart contracts, and digital asset transaction systems.

    • Experience with DevOps practices and tools (CI/CD, automated testing, monitoring).

  • Leadership & Communication:

    • Excellent leadership skills with a history of successfully managing and growing engineering teams.

    • Strong communication skills with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

    • Ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and prioritize effectively across multiple initiatives.

What’s in it for you:

  • Friendly and fun start-up work culture

jobs.title: Data Engineer (Data Platform)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We're looking for a Data Engineer to join our Data Platform team at Coinhako.

Every dashboard, fraud signal, financial report and AI-driven analysis in the company depends on data being right. Our team runs the systems that make that true — the metadata repository, the ingestion and ELT pipelines, the warehouse, and the internal tools our teams use every day.

This is a hands-on contributor role on a small team, working inside a platform direction that's already set. You'll own pieces end to end: a pipeline one week, an internal tool the next, a data-quality problem the week after. Some of it is systems that are already live and depended on — those become yours to run and improve. The rest is new.

Crypto data does not behave. Upstream sources change shape without telling us. Numbers that look wrong are often correct, and numbers that look fine sometimes aren't. Most of the interesting work here is in knowing the difference — and building systems that hold up when you can't be sure.

What you'll be doing:

Write and run pipelines

  • Write and operate ingestion and ELT pipelines (Airflow / MWAA) bringing in transactions, product events and third-party feeds

  • Take a source we've never used and turn it into a table analysts trust

  • Keep pipelines healthy — including ones you didn't write

Contribute to guaranteeing the accuracy of our numbers

  • Add quality checks that stop bad data reaching reports, and make missing data visible instead of silent

  • Reconcile our numbers against independent sources

  • Investigate when a number looks wrong, and be able to say why it was — or wasn't

Contribute to the metadata layer

  • Add to and maintain the metadata repository that pipelines, apps and analytics rely on

  • Document datasets well enough that analysts and AI systems can use them without asking us

Contribute to the internal tools

  • Work on the backend and data layer behind the internal tools our teams depend on — the APIs they call and the metadata that drives them

  • Help integrate AI (LLM / RAG, agentic analysis) into the platform and its tools

Support the people who use it

  • Handle requests from analysts and stakeholders, and turn the repetitive ones into something self-service

What we're looking for:

  • 2–4 years in data engineering, backend, or platform engineering

  • Strong SQL and Python

  • Experience writing and running pipelines with Airflow or something similar

  • Familiarity with cloud services (AWS preferred)

  • You understand the systems you've built — why they behave the way they do, what the trade-offs were, and what they cost to run

  • You've owned something in production end to end — deployed it, looked after it, and fixed it when it broke

  • You verify your own work before you call it done

  • Comfortable in code you didn't write, on systems that are already live

  • Comfortable writing backend code and deploying a service, not only running pipelines

  • Clear communication, and the judgement to flag uncertainty early rather than late

Nice to Have:

  • Financial services, fintech or crypto, and handling sensitive transaction data

  • Shipping and deploying internal tools or services — APIs, jobs, small apps

  • Data-quality tooling — Great Expectations, Soda, dbt tests

  • Experience with data you can't get back — streaming retention windows, APIs with no history, anything where missing the read means the observation never existed

What Success Looks Like:

  • The pipelines you look after run reliably — and when they don't, you know before anyone else does

  • Data-quality problems get caught before they reach a report, a dashboard, or an AI system

  • New sources go live cleanly, and the next one is easier because of how you did the last one

  • Analysts ask fewer repeat questions, because the answer is documented or self-service

  • When something breaks, you can explain what happened, what you changed, and why it won't happen the same way twice

  • AI tooling is expected, and we provide it. We care that you can explain and defend what you shipped — not that you typed every line

What’s in it for you:

  • Friendly and fun start-up work culture

  • Convenient work location located in the heart of CBD area

  • Generous annual leaves on top of national holidays

  • Medical coverage including GP, Specialist, TCM, and more

  • Self-care benefits and exciting fitness workshops/webinars

  • Vibrant office with a well-stocked pantry

Find out more about Coinhako here https://www.coinhako.com/ and don't forget to visit our Careers Page https://www.coinhako.com/join-us

By submitting your application to us, you consent to the collection, use, disclosure and processing of your personal data in accordance with our privacy policy, which is accessible at https://www.coinhako.com/legal/sg-1/privacy_policy.

jobs.title: Finance Intern - Nov Start
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Role

We are looking for a motivated Finance and Accounting Intern to support the day-to-day financial operations of a fast-growing crypto firm. The intern will gain practical exposure to accounting, digital-asset operations, financial reporting and regulatory controls.

What You’ll Do

  • Assist with accounts payable, payment processing, invoice verification and expense tracking.

  • Perform bank, digital wallet and liquidity-provider reconciliations.

  • Support the recording and reconciliation of cryptocurrency transactions, client funds and trading balances.

  • Assist with month-end closing, journal entries and preparation of management reports.

  • Maintain accounting schedules, supporting documents and audit records.

  • Support financial and regulatory reporting, including data extraction and validation.

  • Investigate reconciliation differences and follow up with Finance, Operations and Technology teams.

  • Assist with process improvements, automation and other ad hoc finance projects.

What We’re Looking For

  • Currently pursuing a diploma or degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related discipline.

  • Basic understanding of accounting principles and financial statements.

  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets.

  • Detail-oriented, organised and comfortable working with large volumes of data.

  • Strong communication skills and willingness to work across different teams.

  • Interest in cryptocurrency, digital assets or fintech is preferred, but prior industry experience is not required.

This internship provides hands-on experience in both traditional accounting and the financial operations of a regulated digital-asset business.

What’s in it for you

  • Friendly and fun start-up work culture

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Consensys

Consensys Incorporated is an independent blockchain infrastructure company, spun out of Consensys Software Inc. — one of the world's leading blockchain technology companies and the primary development organization behind the Ethereum ecosystem.

We build and operate neutral, institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure that connects banks, asset managers, custodians, and financial market infrastructures to digital asset networks, meeting the non-negotiable standards of institutional finance: privacy, scalability, resilience, security, and regulatory readiness.

Headquartered in Miami, Florida, and operating across the US, Europe, and Australia, Consensys Incorporated launched as an independent entity in September 2026 and is building the team to match its ambition.

Why this role exists

We build and operate blockchain infrastructure for financial market infrastructure — settlement, custody and clearing institutions who put real value on the networks we run. We have signed clients with production dates this quarter, a platform that has to stand up on its own for the first time, and an engineering organization that has just been through a leadership transition.

You are the engineering leader for that organization — the person who owns what we've committed to ships, and who the engineers look to when a technical decision needs making.

What you'll own

  • The delivery organization — core engineering (sequencer, node and backend services), smart contracts, and infrastructure/DevOps.

  • Client delivery against contractual commitments. Several institutional programs are in flight with production dates between now and Q1, each with availability, latency and evidence requirements written into the contract. Availability definitions, maintenance windows, DR, incident process and the proof behind them are yours. System reliability engineering and on-call rota included.

  • Operating production networks — including a public mainnet run under an arm's-length managed-service agreement, alongside sovereign and permissioned networks for clients.

  • Work with the Security Lead to help set security standards for partners, clients and internal systems.

  • The technical roadmap and its sequencing — working with Product and Sales to define what we build, what we buy, what we say no to, and the honest version of when.

  • Completing the separation from our former parent. Observability, deployment tooling, identity and infrastructure-as-code all have to be rebuilt or properly handed over, under a live clock.

  • Engineering standards and the release process — how we test, how we ship, how we roll back, how we review, and how we maintain.

  • Being a credible technical voice with clients. Our buyers are institutional. They will ask you hard questions about resilience, custody of keys, and what happens at 3am, and they will judge the company by the answer.

  • Leadership and people management — hire, lead, mentor, and develop engineering managers and team leads; foster a remote-first, high-performing, collaborative engineering culture; support performance management and career development; and liaise closely with team leads to coordinate priorities, dependencies, resourcing, and delivery across engineering.

  • Contribute to major architecture or investment proposals.

  • Meet customers or partners where engineering involvement is valuable.

  • Managing and integrating company wide objectives into engineering team based measurable objective key results (OKRs) and communicating on these objectives to the organization.

  • Engineering operating model — who owns what, who decides, and what escalates to you. You set decision rights with Product, Sales and Protocols so a stuck call does not sit in a meeting for two weeks.

  • Delegation. Delivery, incidents and most design calls sit with engineering managers and tech leads. You are the exception path and the person who builds those managers, not doing every estimate and every review.

  • How the organization uses AI in the actual work. You use it yourself every day and you make it the default for the teams, with the same bar we already apply to human-written code. This is practice, not an “AI strategy” slide.

  • Cost management. You will strive to reduce operating costs wherever possible without reducing quality or productivity.

Two lines sit outside this role and you'll work with both constantly:

  • Cryptography and ZK research (prover, zkEVM, arithmetization) reports to the HoE. Their output lands in your release process — prover upgrades, hard-fork integration, mainnet rollout — so the interface matters.

  • Core protocols (Besu, Teku and related clients) sit with our Head of Protocols, reporting to the CEO. Some of your delivery dates depend on their commitments; that relationship is a partnership, not a reporting line.

What we are looking for

  • Deep Ethereum and EVM experience.

  • Has run an engineering team of 20+ across multiple teams, as a leader of leaders — and has done it at this company stage.

  • Has owned production systems under contractual SLAs for demanding customers, and has personally been accountable for an outage in front of one.

  • Deeply technical. You don't need to be the best engineer here, but you need to earn the respect of people who are — challenge a design, know when an estimate is optimistic.

  • Distributed-systems depth. Blockchain experience is a real advantage; strong infrastructure and backend leaders from high-integrity domains (payments, exchanges, market infrastructure) will be taken seriously.

  • Has hired well and retained people through a hard period.

  • Someone with sound technical judgment, strategic thinking, commercial awareness, and strong prioritization skills.

  • Direct. This team has a low tolerance for polish over substance. Say the hard thing early, and say it kindly, more light, less heat.

  • People-first leader — empathetic, approachable, and committed to mentoring and developing others.

  • Strong communicator — builds trust and communicates clearly across engineering and the wider business.

  • Collaborative — works closely with team leads to align priorities, coordinate dependencies, and keep teams moving together.

  • High emotional intelligence — self-aware, thoughtful, and comfortable navigating difficult conversations and change.

  • Coach and multiplier — develops strong leaders, delegates effectively, and builds high-performing, autonomous teams.

  • Pragmatic and organized — brings clarity and structure without unnecessary process.

Useful, not required

  • L2 or ZK-rollup architecture.

  • Regulated financial infrastructure — audit, change control, evidence, SOC 2 / ISO 27001.

  • Experience of a carve-out, separation or post-acquisition integration.

What this role is not

  • Not a box-checker, don’t add process for process sake.

  • Someone who does not challenge or seek clarity.

  • Someone who does not seek to understand why and what the value is for a task.

  • Someone who feels like they have to be the loudest voice in the room and does not seek to listen first and leverage the intelligence of others.

  • Someone who has not had experience managing engineering teams and who feels comfortable being a single IC.

  • A 100% hands-on engineering role.

Working at Consensys

We are a fully remote, globally distributed company. We hire the best people wherever they are, work asynchronously, and judge each other on impact rather than hours or location. We offer competitive compensation, meaningful equity, and the chance to work on genuinely open source software at the frontier of web3.

Consensys is an equal opportunities employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) I
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Consensys

Consensys Incorporated is an independent blockchain infrastructure company, spun out of Consensys Software Inc. — one of the world's leading blockchain technology companies and the primary development organization behind the Ethereum ecosystem.

We build and operate neutral, institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure that connects banks, asset managers, custodians, and financial market infrastructures to digital asset networks, meeting the non-negotiable standards of institutional finance: privacy, scalability, resilience, security, and regulatory readiness.

Headquartered in Miami, Florida, and operating across the US, Europe, and Australia, Consensys Incorporated launched as an independent entity in September 2026 and is building the team to match its ambition.

Why this role exists

Consensys Incorporated operates production blockchain infrastructure for financial institutions. Those networks don't stop at 18:00 CET, and today our infrastructure team sits mostly in Europe. This role closes that gap: you are our engineer on the ground when Europe is asleep.

This is a coverage-first role. Roughly 60% incident response, monitoring and operational hardening; 40% build work on the platform. If you want a pure greenfield engineering job, this isn't it — but you will be the first person in the timezone, which means you help design the rota rather than inherit it.

What you'll own

  • Front-line operational coverage for production networks during APAC hours — monitoring, triage, escalation, and running incidents to resolution.

  • Participation in (and help designing) a follow-the-sun on-call rota alongside the European team, replacing the arrangement we're transitioning off.

  • Deployment and maintenance windows scheduled in APAC hours: node upgrades, chain releases, coordinated maintenance.

  • Runbooks, alert tuning and observability improvements — specifically, turning the things you get paged for into things nobody gets paged for.

  • Platform build work between incidents: Kubernetes, GitOps, IaC, CI/CD pipelines.

  • Being the operational contact for APAC-based client and partner teams.

First 90 days

  1. Ramp on the stack. Realistically this takes three months — Kubernetes, ArgoCD/GitOps, Ethereum clients, the Linea stack (sequencer, coordinator, prover), ZK proving. We will not put you on a pager before you're ready.

  2. Shadow European incidents, then run them.

  3. Take the first APAC on-call shift and write the runbook gaps you find.

What we are looking for

  • 4+ years in DevOps/SRE/platform engineering, including real production on-call for a system with an external SLA.

  • Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code in anger (Terraform or equivalent); GitOps-based deployment.

  • Cloud depth — AWS primarily, Azure useful.

  • Observability as a practice, not a dashboard: Prometheus/Grafana, alerting design, SLIs and error budgets.

  • Comfortable being the only person awake on your continent: escalates early, writes things down, doesn't guess in production.

  • Scripting/automation — Python, Go or Bash.

Useful, not required

  • Ethereum or blockchain node operations (Besu, Geth, Teku, or similar) — we can teach this to a strong infra engineer.

  • Regulated-environment experience: change control, evidence, audit.

  • Java, or experience operating JVM services under load.

What this role is not

Not a 24/7 helpdesk. Not an escalation inbox. You're an engineer who happens to be the first line during your hours, and the expectation is that the operational load falls over time because of work you do.

Working at Consensys

We are a fully remote, globally distributed company. We hire the best people wherever they are, work asynchronously, and judge each other on impact rather than hours or location. We offer competitive compensation, meaningful equity, and the chance to work on genuinely open source software at the frontier of web3.

Consensys is an equal opportunities employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Software / Systems Architect
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Consensys

Consensys Incorporated is an independent blockchain infrastructure company, spun out of Consensys Software Inc. — one of the world's leading blockchain technology companies and the primary development organization behind the Ethereum ecosystem.

We build and operate neutral, institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure that connects banks, asset managers, custodians, and financial market infrastructures to digital asset networks, meeting the non-negotiable standards of institutional finance: privacy, scalability, resilience, security, and regulatory readiness.

Headquartered in Miami, Florida, and operating across the US, Europe, and Australia, Consensys Incorporated launched as an independent entity in September 2026 and is building the team to match its ambition.

Why this role exists

We build and operate blockchain infrastructure for financial market infrastructure — settlement, custody and clearing institutions. The platform spans a sequencer and coordinator, a ZK proving stack, cross-ledger interoperability, privacy and settlement components, and the infrastructure that runs all of it in production for clients with contractual commitments.

Someone has to hold that whole picture and make the pieces fit. Not in a diagram — in the code, in the design decisions, and in the answers we give institutional architects who are deciding whether to put real value on our networks.

This is a hands-on role. You will write code, build proofs of concept, and be in the design reviews. If you haven't shipped something yourself in the last year, this isn't the right role.

What you'll own

  • Architecture across the platform — how the sequencer, coordinator, proving stack, interop layer, privacy components and infrastructure fit together, and where the seams are.

  • Cross-ledger interoperability architecture. This is our differentiator and our IP, not a commodity — the design choices here decide what we can sell and what we can charge for.

  • Turning institutional requirements into designs. Our clients issue detailed requirement documents — availability, finality, privacy isolation, RBAC, key custody, emergency deployment. You turn those into architecture the team can build and we can evidence, and you are honest about which requirements we meet technically and which we meet by control and attestation.

  • Proofs of concept. Built by you in partnership with the Engineering team, after specified to a high quality by you. Ambiguity gets resolved by building the smallest real thing.

  • Design reviews and architecture decisions — written down, with the reasoning and the discarded options, so the next person doesn't re-litigate them.

  • Build versus buy. Where we take a third-party component, where we build, and what that costs us in dependency.

  • Technical depth in client and partner deep-dives when the conversation goes past what a slide can carry.

  • Architecture decisions are final. You time-box spikes and PoCs, you write down the discarded path, and you freeze the call so engineering is not implementing two designs at once.

  • You own the design so other people can build. That means interfaces, constraints and written decisions — not sitting in every review. Teams should be able to ship against an Architecture Decision Record without you in the room.

  • You use AI daily to explore designs, write and test PoCs and draft ADRs. You set that practice for the people who implement your designs.

  • Designs that survive production. Availability, finality, rollback and proving upgrades are architecture constraints, not an ops surprise after merge.

How this fits

  • Product — you pair closely with Product on what we build and why. Architecture that isn't anchored in a client problem is a hobby.

  • Cryptography and ZK research (prover, zkEVM, arithmetization) — a separate line. Their output is a major input to your architecture; you need enough depth to reason about proving costs, latency and constraints without needing to be a cryptographer.

  • Core protocols (Besu, Teku and related clients) — sits with our Head of Protocols. Client capabilities and roadmap commitments there shape what you can design.

  • Engineering and infrastructure — your designs are built and operated by these teams. They will tell you quickly if a design doesn't survive contact with production, and you should want them to.

What we are looking for

  • Has designed distributed systems and built them — recent, hands-on, in a language we use (Kotlin, Go, Rust, Solidity, TypeScript, Zig).

  • Has strong hands-on background of Software Development/Engineering, 8+ years.

  • Can hold a large system in their head and see where it doesn't fit together, and reason down to detailed technical level— the failure modes, the coupling, the thing that breaks at scale–and be able to effectively communicate this to colleagues.

  • Ethereum and EVM knowledge, or the demonstrated ability to get there fast from adjacent distributed-systems work.

  • Writes clearly. Design documents and diagrams that a bank's architecture team will accept without a meeting. Not just for external, but for internal too. The architect should leave behind clear written artifacts that make it clear what engineers need to build and why, and what success looks like.

  • Can be in a room with institutional architects and stay technical — credible on resilience, key custody, finality and privacy without drifting into sales language.

  • Pragmatic. Knows when the right architecture is the boring one.

  • Decisive under ambiguity. Makes the call when Product, a client requirement and a protocol constraint disagree.

  • Experience architecting for secure mission-critical systems.

Useful, not required

  • ZK proof systems — enough to reason about cost, latency and trust assumptions.

  • Privacy technologies: privacy pools, MPC, trusted execution, tokenisation frameworks.

  • Regulated financial infrastructure — payments, clearing, settlement, custody.

  • Understanding of governance dynamics and key stakeholders within the Ethereum ecosystem.

  • Experience of cloud and infra deployments and topologies.

  • Experience in Fintech/Banking/Trading or similar domains.

What this role is not

  • Not a PowerPoint architect. If the last two years of your work are diagrams and decks, this is the wrong role and the interview will find that out.

  • Not a pre-sales function. You'll join client technical sessions, but delivery is the job.

  • Not a people-management role. This is an individual contributor position with real technical authority.

Working at Consensys

We are a fully remote, globally distributed company. We hire the best people wherever they are, work asynchronously, and judge each other on impact rather than hours or location. We offer competitive compensation, meaningful equity, and the chance to work on genuinely open source software at the frontier of web3.

Consensys is an equal opportunities employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.
