jobs.title: Menlo Fellows
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The Role
Menlo builds open source and production AI systems, from the brain, to developer facing tools to the runtime infrastructure and humanoid platform underneath. This fellowship is deliberately open ended: tell us your strengths and we'll match you to high impact work across software engineering, systems, applied AI, or research. You'll be hands on from day one, with a Menlo engineer or researcher directly responsible for your mentorship and your results. You own deliverables at the same level as the team you join. We expect you to contribute, not observe.

This is a paid internship program that runs year round. Candidates go through a rigorous interview process and get matched with a senior researcher or engineer working on real world problems.

What You'll Do

  • Own a real project end to end, from problem definition through implementation, testing, and documentation.

  • Ship production grade work in one or more areas: product engineering, systems, infrastructure, applied AI, or research.

  • Work on core Menlo projects, including developer tooling, model runtime and performance, automation, and reliability improvements.

  • Debug real issues across codebases and environments, and propose fixes that improve correctness, performance, and maintainability.

  • Write clear docs, runbooks, or internal notes that make your work easy for the team to adopt.

  • Collaborate closely with engineers and researchers through code reviews and technical discussions.


What We Look For

  • University, high school or mid-career individuals looking for a crash course in physical AI and robotics

  • The ability to read unfamiliar codebases and make safe, well scoped changes.

  • Practical debugging skills: you can isolate problems and validate fixes.

jobs.title: Researcher, World Models
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

We are hiring a Researcher to advance the world models at the core of Asimov's ability to perceive, predict, and act. You will work at the intersection of self-supervised representation learning, predictive architectures, and embodied control, in close collaboration with our platform, firmware, and hardware teams.

What You'll Do

  • Design, train, and rigorously evaluate world models that let Asimov predict the consequences of actions across visual, proprioceptive, and force/torque modalities.

  • Advance our self-supervised learning stack for visual and sensor representations, building on and extending the JEPA family (V-JEPA, I-JEPA, and related predictive-embedding approaches).

  • Prototype and benchmark generative and predictive architectures (diffusion, DiT, flow matching, VAEs) against JEPA-style objectives for embodied prediction and planning.

  • Own the data pipeline for your experiments end to end: curation, tooling, and scaling, without depending on a separate data-engineering team to move.

  • Integrate what you build with our platform, firmware, and software teams so research reaches the robot, not just the paper.

  • Contribute to sim-to-real transfer, inverse dynamics, and multi-modal sensor fusion, and publish or open-source work where it strengthens the field and the team.

What We Look For

  • Proven modeling track record: you have trained models and can show solid, honest evaluations, not just training curves.

  • JEPA fluency: you understand the joint-embedding predictive approach and can reason about where it fits versus alternatives.

  • Breadth across approaches: familiarity with prior and adjacent work, including VLA (vision-language-action) models, and a view on their trade-offs.

  • Depth in a modality: strong depth in at least one sensory domain (vision, audio, natural language, or similar).

  • Strong data abilities: you get things done without depending on a whole data-engineering team.

  • Solid engineering: you can implement, integrate, and ship what you build alongside platform, firmware, and software teams.

  • Conversant, ideally deep, in several of: SSL for visual and sensor representations; world models (JEPA, V-JEPA, I-JEPA, LeJEPA, MJEPA); generative and predictive architectures (diffusion, DiT, flow matching, VAEs); robotics ML (VLA, inverse dynamics, sim-to-real, optical flow); sensor fusion (vision, proprioception, force/torque, multi-modal encoders); PyTorch, JAX, and distributed training.

Nice to Have

  • Publications at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, or RSS (or arXiv work with comparable citations).

  • PhD or equivalent research experience in ML, robotics, or computer vision. Not required with a strong portfolio.

  • Demonstrated hardware or robotics interest or hands-on experience.

  • Strong communication: technical blogs, talks, or clear written research.

Why Join Menlo

World models are the bet that lets a humanoid generalize instead of memorize. This is a rare seat where your research runs on real hardware in short cycles, your data and modeling choices are yours to own, and your work ships in the open. If you want the distance between an idea and a walking robot to be measured in weeks, this is the room.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Jan

Jan is an open source AI assistant built by Menlo. It began as a private, offline alternative to ChatGPT and has grown into a general purpose agent that runs open models locally on your own hardware, or connects to frontier models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini when you want them. Give Jan a task and it works on its own until the job is done. Built in public around one belief: AI should be open, private, and answer only to you.

The Role

We are building Jan Router, an enterprise LLM gateway. Think OpenRouter, but for organizations: one gateway in front of many model providers that routes traffic intelligently and gives an org a single place to manage keys, budgets, quotas, usage, and billing. You will bootstrap it from scratch and own the architecture, the first production deploy, and everything from the request proxy to the billing ledger. This is a lean, agent-native setup. Rather than leaning on a large team, you will orchestrate coding and execution agents to ship at team-scale velocity, while keeping the hard backend judgment to build a billing-grade gateway that does not fall over. The router is your primary charge, but not your only one: you will also contribute to the Jan Agent, wiring agent and tool traffic through the same routing, metering, and controls. You are fluent in trade-offs. You know which parts can ship fast and be hardened later, and which parts, like the money path and auth, have to be right the first time. This role suits a Backend or Software Engineer ready to open a new chapter: working closely with a frontier research team and building real AI services from the bottom up, starting at the model level.

What You'll Do

  • Build the core gateway: a unified, OpenAI-compatible API in front of multiple providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, plus self-hosted and OSS models).

  • Own provider routing and reliability: load balancing, automatic failover, and cost and latency-aware routing.

  • Build billing and metering that is correct, not approximate: per-request token accounting, usage ledgers, cost attribution per team, user, and key, budgets, and spend limits.

  • Ship org controls: API key management, per-team and per-user quotas, rate limiting, and RBAC.

  • Handle streaming and performance: low-overhead proxying, streaming responses, connection handling, and caching where it helps.

  • Contribute to the Jan Agent and connect it to the router: route its model and tool calls through the gateway, and make agent traffic first-class in metering, controls, and observability.

  • Make deliberate speed-versus-correctness calls: move fast where iteration is cheap, refuse to cut corners where a bug means a bad charge or a leaked key, and pay down debt on your own initiative.

What We Look For

  • Work agent-natively as your default, running multiple agents in parallel, pushing token throughput hard, with your own review and guardrail discipline, using open harnesses like Pi, Hermes Agent, and OpenCode as your daily drivers, on open and frontier models alike.

  • Acquainted with LLM API systems: providers, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, streaming, tool calling, and token accounting.

  • Experience with LLM infra: inference proxies, provider SDKs, token counting, or existing gateways and routing services (LiteLLM, cliproxyapi, 9router, Omnirouter, and similar) as reference points.

  • Acquainted with core AI concepts: context windows, inference, prompting, evals, and how open models differ from hosted providers in practice.

  • Proven ability to ship from zero to production and own the result, including infra, deploy, alerting, and CI/CD, regardless of which stack you did it in.

  • Open-minded and pragmatic: you weigh speed against correctness case by case, hold strong opinions loosely, and change course when the evidence says so, all while staying fast-moving and comfortable with full ownership and ambiguity.

Nice to Have

  • A track record building production backend services that handle real traffic: APIs, auth, data modeling, deploy, and monitoring.

  • Experience with payments, billing, metering, or usage-based systems, or the rigor to build them correctly (idempotency, reconciliation, no dropped or double charges).

  • Comfort with high-throughput proxying, gateways, and streaming, and the performance concerns that come with them.

  • Solid datastore skills: PostgreSQL, Redis, queues where needed, and sound schema design for usage and billing data.

  • Strong in at least one of TypeScript or Python.

  • Comfort with Docker, Kubernetes, OAuth and OIDC, API keys, RBAC, tenant isolation, and secure secrets handling.

  • Familiarity with the Jan.ai ecosystem or other OSS LLM tooling.

  • MCP and tool-calling knowledge, directly relevant since you will help the router carry the Jan Agent's agent and tool traffic.

  • Go or Rust for high-performance proxying, not required.

  • Contributions to open agent tooling or harnesses: a Pi extension, a Hermes skill, an OpenCode plugin, or anything in the open-models ecosystem we can look at.

Why Join Menlo

Jan is open-source, built in public, and already in the hands of millions. You will own a real product end to end, work shoulder to shoulder with a frontier research team, drive agents hard to ship at a pace a traditional team cannot match, and set the bar for how a lean, agent-native backend gets built. If you want to be in the arena shipping something that matters, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

The Role
We are looking for an Application Engineer to build and ship the Jan desktop app across platforms. You will own the application end to end, from architecture through packaging and distribution, working full stack across the web and native layers.
This is a build-and-ship role, not a UI design one. You will care about how the app is put together, how it performs, and how cleanly it gets into users' hands on every platform. This is a lean, agent-native setup, so you will orchestrate coding and execution agents to move fast while keeping the judgment to get the hard parts right.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain the Jan desktop app across macOS, Windows, and Linux using Tauri.

  • Work full stack across the app: React and Node.js on the application layer, Rust on the native side.

  • Own packaging, builds, and distribution: installers, auto-update, release pipelines, and code signing.

  • Give Linux first-class support: packaging and distribution across common distros.

  • Integrate local model runtimes and app features end to end.

  • Work agent-natively as your default, running agents in parallel with your own review and guardrail discipline.


What We Look For

  • Full-stack engineer, strong in React and Node.js.

  • Hands-on experience building and shipping Tauri apps.

  • Working knowledge of Rust.

  • Desktop app development and cross-platform distribution experience.

  • Solid Linux skills: packaging, distribution, and environment quirks.

  • Proven ownership of app packaging, builds, and release pipelines.

  • An agent-native default workflow and the judgment to hand-write critical code when it matters.

  • Comfortable with full ownership, ambiguity, and shipping fast.


Nice to Have

jobs.title: Industrial Designer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

Industrial design at Menlo is not cosmetic. Asimov is a physical product that will be assembled, operated, serviced, and iterated on, and how it looks, feels, and reads to the people around it is as consequential as how it performs. As our Industrial Designer, you will own the form language and physical identity of Asimov, from enclosures and surface treatments to ergonomics, CMF (color, material, finish), and packaging. You will translate that vision into parts that manufacture, assemble, and survive the real world, working shoulder to shoulder with mechanical and electrical engineers so every design decision holds up in production. This is design that ships to real hardware, not renders.

What You'll Do

  • Own industrial design for Asimov and the Menlo hardware family: form, proportion, ergonomics, and CMF, from concept and form language to production-ready enclosures, covers, and structural aesthetics

  • Turn mechanical and electrical constraints into clean, intentional design that does not hide the engineering

  • Prototype fast in foam, print, and machined parts, then iterate on real robots to test design intent

  • Own the CMF specification process: material selection, surface finish standards, color systems, and supplier engagement, and make sure those choices hold up in the field

  • Own design for manufacturing and assembly alongside mechanical engineering: DFM reviews, tolerance stack-ups, fastening, serviceability, part count, and assembly sequencing, catching issues before tooling

  • Design the human-facing details: grips, handles, access panels, indicators, and anything a person touches or reads

  • Shape the packaging and unboxing experience and user-facing documentation for Asimov kits and development hardware

  • Maintain design consistency across the Menlo hardware product family as the portfolio expands

What We Look For

  • A strong portfolio of shipped physical products, ideally complex electromechanical hardware, showing a consistent design sensibility under real technical constraints

  • 4 or more years shipping physical products: consumer electronics, robotics, medical devices, or similarly complex hardware

  • Deep industrial design fundamentals: form, proportion, ergonomics, and CMF

  • Strong proficiency in 3D modeling and surfacing (Alias, Rhino, SolidWorks, or equivalent) and rendering (KeyShot or similar), plus real DFM and DFA experience

  • Working knowledge of manufacturing processes: injection molding, sheet metal, die casting, and surface finishing

  • Experience working directly with mechanical engineers and contract manufacturers in a fast, iterative environment

  • Comfort moving from sketch to prototype to production without needing a large team around you

  • Experience designing for humanoid or legged robots, cobots, or other electromechanical systems

  • A bias for building, testing on hardware, and iterating quickly, with the judgment to know when to obsess over a detail and when to ship

Nice to Have

  • Experience taking a product from zero to first production run

  • Hands-on shop skills: 3D printing, machining, moldmaking, and finishing

  • Exposure to DFM/DFA review in a high-mix, low-volume manufacturing context

  • Familiarity with simulation-driven or CAD-driven design workflows

  • A feel for how design and brand reinforce each other

  • Interest in open-source hardware communities

Why Join Menlo

You will define what a humanoid robot looks like at the moment the category is being written. That is a rare brief at this stage of a company, and it comes with the autonomy to match. Your work ships to real machines, in the real world, fast, alongside a small team that moves fast and takes the craft seriously. If you want your design to live in hardware people actually use rather than a slide, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.title: Founding Research Partnerships Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
This is a founding go-to-market role for Asimov in the US research market. You will establish Asimov inside leading US university labs, AI research organizations, and corporate R&D groups, owning a regional territory end to end: first technical conversation, demonstration, purchase, deployment handoff, and expansion. It is not a conventional account-executive role, and not a conventional developer-relations role. You should be able to discuss a researcher's work at a technical level, translate that work into robot hardware, software, data, AI model, and support requirements, then lead the institution through evaluation and procurement.

What You'll Do

  • Build and own a territory of university AI and robotics labs, corporate research organizations, and physical-AI startups.

  • Develop direct relationships with lab directors, principal investigators, research scientists, AI engineers, data teams, and corporate R&D leaders.

  • Run technical discovery around each customer's research objectives, existing robotics and ML stack, data requirements, model-development workflow, training/fine-tuning/sim environment, support needs, and decision process.

  • Determine whether Asimov is the right platform, and recommend the right robot configuration, accessories, software interfaces, data-collection tools, services, and initial deployment.

  • Transport, set up, operate, and demonstrate Asimov at customer labs, conferences, workshops, campus roadshows, and private events.

  • Convert successful initial deployments into larger lab, department, corporate R&D, and multi-site purchases.

  • Bring requirements and competitive feedback back into Menlo's product, engineering, manufacturing, support, and docs teams.

  • Represent Menlo credibly across the physical-AI, embodied-AI, robotics, and academic-research communities and conferences.

What We Look For

  • Demonstrated experience producing paid commercial adoption inside AI labs, robotics labs, corporate AI research groups, or closely comparable technical R&D organizations.

  • Technical fluency to discuss:

    • ROS 2, Linux, Python, networking, and robot software integration

    • perception, control, manipulation, locomotion, and sensor interfaces

    • VLMs, VLAs, world models, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and policy deployment

    • teleoperation, demonstration collection, robotics datasets, simulation, and sim-to-real workflows

    • on-robot or edge inference, latency, compute constraints, and hardware/software tradeoffs

  • Comfort working hands-on with physical robots: setting up demonstrations, diagnosing ordinary problems, and escalating deeper engineering issues with useful technical context.

  • Ability and willingness to travel frequently within your assigned US territory.

  • Technical public-presentation experience.

Nice to Have

  • Prior engineering or research work in robotics, machine learning, embodied AI, autonomous systems, computer vision, controls, or a related domain.

  • Existing relationships with university robotics labs, AI labs, corporate research teams, or physical-AI startups.

  • Experience selling into the robotics ecosystem: hardware, research infrastructure, AI compute, simulation, data platforms, developer tools, or other products used by technical research organizations.

  • Contributions to open-source robotics or ML projects, technical talks, publications, workshops, tutorials, or other evidence of research-community credibility.

This Role Probably Isn't For You If

  • Your experience is primarily conventional SaaS sales without technical research customers.

  • You are a strong roboticist but do not enjoy prospecting, asking qualification questions, discussing money, or creating urgency.

  • You would rather present software demos than operate and troubleshoot real hardware.

Why Join Menlo
You will be the first person carrying Asimov into the US research market, with the freedom to build the territory the way it should be built. Menlo designs its robot in the open, with the people who build on it, and this role puts you at the center of that: shaping how the next generation of labs and R&D teams adopt an open, modular humanoid platform. If you want to be the technical face of a physical-AI company inside the rooms where the research actually happens, this is the seat.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.title: E-Commerce Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
We are hiring our first E-commerce Lead to launch and own shop.menlo.ai from zero to one.
Menlo builds in public, and our community of developers, builders, and robotics fans wants to wear it, carry it, and be part of it. Companies like 1X and Figure have shown how a great store turns a robotics brand into something people can hold. We want ours to be better, and we want one person to own the whole thing. This is a founding, full-stack commerce role. You will pick the platform, build the storefront, source the products, set up fulfillment, run the launches, and own the numbers. You will start with merch and community products. Because Asimov is open, modular, and built with a right to repair, you will also have a path to grow the store into kits, spare parts, and hardware components over time. If you have wanted to build a store end to end, with real creative range and a brand people already love, this is it.

What You'll Do

  • Stand up shop.menlo.ai from scratch, including platform selection, storefront build, checkout, payments, and tax setup across Singapore, Vietnam, the US, and international customers

  • Build the first product line with our brand and design team, from apparel and accessories to limited drops that reflect the Menlo and Asimov identity

  • Own merchandising and the launch calendar, including pricing, product mix, seasonal drops, and tie-ins with product launches and community moments

  • Set up and manage fulfillment, from print on demand and 3PL partners to inventory, packaging, and global shipping

  • Own the store P&L, including margins, unit economics, and forecasting, and report on what is working

  • Drive growth and conversion through analytics, email and lifecycle flows, landing pages, and merchandising experiments

  • Run customer experience end to end, including support, returns, and the post purchase journey

  • Partner with DevRel, community, and supply chain to plan the path from merch into Asimov kits, spare parts, and modular components

  • Represent the store voice so every touchpoint feels like Menlo: open, technical, and built in public


What We Look For

  • Proven experience launching or running a direct to consumer store, ideally on Shopify, and taking it from setup to steady operation

  • A generalist who can move across merchandising, operations, and growth without waiting for a bigger team

  • Comfort with zero to one, where you make the call, ship it, and iterate

  • Solid grasp of fulfillment and logistics, including 3PL, print on demand, inventory, and cross border shipping

  • Data fluency, so pricing, margin, and conversion decisions are grounded in numbers

  • Strong brand and product taste, with an eye for what a technical, design-led audience will actually want


Nice to Have

  • Shopify Plus experience, or hands on comfort with themes, apps, and Liquid

  • Existing relationships with print on demand and 3PL vendors

  • Experience selling physical or hardware products, including spare parts or kit style catalogs

  • Merch or community commerce experience for a developer, gaming, or open source brand

  • Genuine interest in robotics, open source, and building in public


Why Join Menlo
This is your store to build, not a queue of tickets. You will own a surface end to end, for a brand people already love and a community of developers who want to represent it. The range is real: you go from shipping the first t-shirt to shaping how we sell kits, parts, and hardware down the line. If you want to turn a brand people love into something they can hold, this is where it happens.

jobs.title: Researcher, Locomotion
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

We are looking for a Researcher, Locomotion to push Asimov from walking to running, recovering, and moving through the real world with the confidence of something alive. Asimov 0 was built to learn locomotion and Asimov 1 to learn whole-body control, and you will own the policies that make that motion robust on real hardware. You will not stop at a clip in simulation. You will get your work onto a physical biped and keep pushing until it holds up under contact, disturbance, and terrain we did not train for.

What You'll Do

  • Design, train, and ship reinforcement learning policies for bipedal and whole-body locomotion on Asimov

  • Own the sim2real pipeline end to end, building on our zero-shot sim2real work so a first run on hardware is never really a first run

  • Push balance, gait, and recovery behavior past the demo stage into something that survives pushes, slips, and uneven ground

  • Build and refine reward design, domain randomization, and training environments in MuJoCo

  • Close the loop between simulation and hardware with real telemetry from real robots, then feed what breaks back into the next policy

  • Work shoulder to shoulder with hardware, controls, and manipulation researchers, since whole-body control does not respect team boundaries

  • Open-source what you can and write up what you learn so the community can build on it

What We Look For

  • Deep hands-on experience with reinforcement learning for continuous control, legged locomotion, or whole-body control

  • A track record of getting learned policies onto real robots, not only into papers or simulators

  • Strong command of a physics simulator such as MuJoCo, Isaac, or similar, including reward shaping and domain randomization

  • Fluency in Python and modern RL tooling, and comfort in a ROS2-based control stack

  • A bias for shipping: you would rather see a policy stumble on real hardware this week than look perfect in sim next month

  • Clear thinking about why a policy fails, not just whether it does

Nice to Have

  • Published work in locomotion, legged robotics, or sim2real transfer

  • Experience with model predictive control or classical locomotion methods alongside learning-based approaches

  • Contributions to open-source robotics or RL projects

  • Experience bringing up new hardware and debugging the messy gap between a model and a motor

Why Join Menlo

The Role
We are hiring a Designer to own how Menlo looks and feels across our website, our communications, and everything in between. Menlo builds in public, and the brand is a big part of why people love Asimov. Every launch, research post, careers page, and community moment is a chance to show the world what we are building. We want one designer who can own that whole surface, from the marketing site to the social asset that goes out an hour before a demo.
This is a broad, hands-on design role for someone who moves fast and has real range. You will shape the brand system, design the pages, and turn around the comms assets, all while keeping Menlo and Asimov looking sharp and consistent.
If you want to own the look of a company people are already watching, this is it.

What You'll Do

  • Own the visual design of menlo.ai and its surfaces, from marketing and launch pages to the careers page and shop touchpoints, working with engineering to ship them to production

  • Design communications assets across every launch, including social posts, announcement art, research post graphics, video thumbnails, and event and IRL collateral

  • Build and maintain the Menlo brand system, including typography, color, and reusable components and templates, so the whole team can move fast and stay on brand

  • Keep Menlo and Asimov visually consistent across the website, docs, community channels, and partner materials

  • Design decks, one-pagers, and collateral for sales, partnerships, and hiring

  • Design for the build in public motion across Discord, the forum, streams, and community moments

  • Turn rough ideas into finished work quickly, often on launch-day timelines


What We Look For

  • A strong portfolio that spans brand, web, and communications design, not just one of the three

  • Real range, from setting up a brand system to designing a marketing site to shipping fast-turn social assets

  • Comfort owning brand at an early company, where you set the bar rather than inherit it

  • Fluency in Figma and a sharp eye for layout, type, and detail

  • Web design sensibility, including responsive thinking and a smooth handoff or collaboration with engineers

  • Taste for a technical, developer-facing aesthetic that feels clean and confident, never corporate

  • Self-direction and speed, with a bias for shipping


Nice to Have

  • Front-end skills such as HTML, CSS, Tailwind, or React and Next.js, enough to ship your own designs to production

  • Motion design or video editing for launches and social

  • Illustration or 3D skills, such as Blender, for robots and hardware

  • Photography or art direction for product and team shoots

  • Experience at a hardware, robotics, developer tools, or open source brand

jobs.title: Deployment Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
The hard problem in robotics is not building a compelling prototype. It is making robotic systems deployable, repeatable, and economically useful in the real world. You will work directly on real customer problems, but you will not stop at integration or customization. You will use deployment pressure to uncover missing capabilities, design evaluations, collect data, adapt models, and turn one-off field learnings into reusable product and research improvements.
This is not a support role. It is not solutions engineering. It is a deployment-native R&D role for people who want to stay close to reality and build the abstractions that make the next deployment easier.

What You'll Do

  • Own real customer and deployment problems end to end, from understanding the workflow to diagnosing failures in the field

  • Work directly with robotic systems in commercial and industrial environments where variability, ambiguity, and operational constraints are the norm

  • Translate deployment friction into research and product questions: what capability is missing, what data is needed, what evaluation should exist, what part of the stack must improve

  • Build and adapt systems across the deployment loop, including data collection, task-specific fine-tuning, and evaluation design

  • Collaborate closely with core research and platform teams so field learnings become reusable capabilities instead of one-off fixes

  • Contribute domain expertise to a broader forward deployment practice where knowledge is shared across deployments and specializations

  • Help define the operating model for how humanoid systems are deployed, improved, and scaled


What We're Looking For

  • Deep expertise in at least one relevant technical domain: perception, navigation, manipulation, or teleoperation

  • Experience deploying AI, robotics, or embodied systems in real environments rather than only in lab settings

  • Comfortable working outside your specialization when the deployment demands it

  • Experience collecting, cleaning, or curating deployment data for model improvement

  • Experience designing evaluations or benchmarks for systems that interact with real-world environments

  • Able to explain complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences

  • Energized by ambiguity, motivated by ownership, and wants to see work survive contact with the real world


Nice to Have

  • Comfort moving between software, research, operations, and user conversations as needed

  • Evidence of building trust with users while maintaining a strong technical point of view

  • Prior experience in a forward deployed or customer-facing technical role at a fast-moving company


Why Join Menlo?
You will sit at the point where all of Menlo's core systems come together: the agent platform, simulation infrastructure, motor control and policy training, the Asimov reference platform, and the data engine. If you join as a Deployment Engineer, you will not just fill a role. You will help define a category. If you want to do serious technical work, stay close to real deployments, and invent the operating model for deployable robotic systems, we would love to talk.

jobs.title: Product Quality Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
Asimov gets built at scale on someone else's line. As Product Quality Engineer, you are Menlo's quality owner at our contract manufacturer, responsible for the final assembly and test of the robot from the first trial build through mass production. You make sure what comes off the CM line matches what our engineers designed, every unit, at rate.
You will own process yield, define and enforce final inspection criteria, and run the customer side of quality at the EMS partner. You will live in the phase gates, EVT, DVT, PVT, and into MP, catching the defects, drift, and process gaps that decide whether a ramp succeeds or stalls. This role sits between our design teams and the factory floor, and holds both to the standard.

What You'll Do

  • Own final assembly and test quality at the CM (Tier-1 / EMS), from trial production through mass production

  • Drive process yield: monitor first-pass yield and defect rates at each station, run the analysis, and lead the CM to close the gaps

  • Define, document, and maintain final inspection criteria, including inspection standards, limit samples, workmanship standards, and pass/fail criteria for the line

  • Own the customer inspection and acceptance process: OQC, outgoing quality gates, AQL sampling plans, and lot disposition before shipment

  • Represent Menlo through the NPI phase gates (EVT, DVT, PVT), driving build readiness, defining test coverage at final assembly and test, and signing off on quality exit criteria for each phase

  • Lead root cause analysis and corrective action on line failures and test escapes, using structured methods such as 8D, fishbone, and 5-whys, and verify the fix holds

  • Set up and audit the CM's process controls: FAI, in-process inspection, SPC on critical parameters, and change control on the line

  • Manage non-conformance at the CM: MRB, containment, rework and sorting decisions, and disposition of held material

  • Track and report quality metrics (yield, DPPM, defect Pareto, RTY) and drive continuous improvement reviews with the CM

  • Partner with mechanical, electrical, firmware, and manufacturing engineering to feed field and line failures back into design and process


What We Look For

  • 3 or more years in a product, supplier, or manufacturing quality role owning final assembly and test at a contract manufacturer or EMS partner

  • Direct experience taking a product through NPI phase gates (EVT / DVT / PVT) and into mass production

  • Strong command of yield analysis and defect reduction, and the discipline to chase a failure to its real source rather than its symptom

  • Hands-on ownership of final inspection and outgoing quality: inspection criteria, AQL sampling, limit samples, and lot acceptance

  • Fluency in core quality tools and methods: 8D, FMEA, SPC, control plans, FAI, and MRB / non-conformance handling

  • Comfort reading mechanical drawings and GD&T, electrical schematics, and test specs across a complex electromechanical product

  • Strong communication and influence skills to hold a CM accountable while keeping the ramp moving, working across engineering, manufacturing, and the supplier

  • Willingness to travel to and work on-site at manufacturing partners


Nice to Have

  • Experience with robotics, automotive, aerospace, medical devices, or other high-reliability electromechanical products

  • Experience managing quality at CMs in the region (for example Vietnam, China, or elsewhere in Asia)

  • Familiarity with quality systems and standards such as ISO 9001, APQP, PPAP, and IPC-A-610

  • Motor, actuator, or drivetrain assembly and test quality experience

  • Experience defining final assembly and test (FATP) test coverage and station-level test strategy

  • Scripting for quality data analysis and automation, for example Python or SQL

  • Experience standing up CM quality processes from near-zero at an early-stage hardware company


Why Join Menlo
You will own the quality of a humanoid robot as it moves from a handful of hand-built prototypes to real production volume, the phase where most hardware companies either learn to ship or quietly stall. You will define the inspection standards and yield discipline for a product that has to move in the real world, not pass a bench check, and you will hold both our engineers and our factory to them. On a small team, your sign-off is what stands between a design and a shippable robot.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. jobs.title: Firmware Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
You own the software that sits closest to Asimov's hardware, the code that closes control loops on time, every time. You work from bare-metal joint controllers up through embedded Linux on the robot's compute platform, bringing up new boards, writing drivers for the sensors and actuators that make the robot move, and making sure the timing guarantees the controls and autonomy teams depend on actually hold on real hardware.

What You'll Do

  • Design, implement, and test real-time firmware in C/C++ for joint controllers, sensor boards, and power management across the robot

  • Own the embedded Linux platform on Asimov's onboard compute: kernel configuration, device drivers, device trees, and board support packages

  • Bring up new board revisions alongside the electrical team, from first power-on to a fully characterized, controllable subsystem

  • Build and maintain the communication layer between joints and the main compute stack, including bus scheduling, time synchronization, and the joint-level API exposed to controls

  • Own bootloader, flashing, and firmware update flows across every board on the robot, so a fleet-wide update is routine rather than an event

  • Integrate sensors, including IMUs, encoders, force-torque, and camera interfaces, with correct timestamping and deterministic latency

  • Implement safety and fault handling: watchdogs, E-stop paths, thermal and current limits, and graceful degradation when a subsystem drops out

  • Debug across the hardware-software boundary with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and bus sniffers, and build the test automation that catches regressions before they reach a robot

  • Contribute to Menlo's open-source efforts, including firmware, drivers, and hardware bring-up documentation for the broader robotics community


What We Look For

  • 3 or more years of hands-on firmware or embedded software experience on products that ship and run in the real world

  • Strong C and C++ in resource-constrained, real-time environments, plus Python for tooling, test automation, and calibration scripts

  • Practical embedded Linux experience: kernel and driver work, device trees, cross-compilation toolchains, and a build system such as Yocto or Buildroot

  • Solid grounding in real-time systems: interrupt latency, scheduling, jitter, priority inversion, and the discipline to measure timing rather than assume it

  • Deep familiarity with hardware interfaces including SPI, I2C, CAN, UART, and camera interfaces such as MIPI CSI-2 or GMSL

  • Comfort reading schematics and datasheets, and debugging with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG/SWD, and bus analyzers

  • Strong communication skills to drive alignment across electrical, mechanical, and controls teams


Nice to Have

  • Experience with bipedal or humanoid robots, legged locomotion platforms, or other high-DOF electromechanical systems

  • Motor control firmware experience: FOC commutation, current/velocity/position loops, encoder calibration, and fault protection

  • RTOS experience (Zephyr, FreeRTOS) or PREEMPT_RT and real-time tuning on Linux

  • Time-sensitive networking, or other deterministic fieldbus and distributed clock synchronization

  • Secure boot, signed images, and over-the-air update infrastructure

  • Familiarity with ROS 2 and how firmware-level data reaches the autonomy stack

  • Hardware-in-the-loop test rigs and CI for firmware

  • Board bring-up experience across multiple hardware revisions of the same product


Why Join Menlo
We are a physical AI company building real robots, and your code is what makes them move. You own the layer closest to the hardware, ship to real robots on a short loop, and open-source what you can for the community building on Asimov. It is a small team with a huge surface area, which means real ownership and the chance to watch your work stand up and walk.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
Own visual storytelling at Menlo. Develop ideas and bring them to life, from everyday lab footage to full launch productions. Help people understand what we're building and care about what they can do with it.

What You'll Do

  • Create videos around product releases, engineering progress, and customer projects.

  • Bring original ideas and take them through production.

  • Give our content a consistent look and feel.

  • Spend time with the technical team to understand what's worth showing and why it matters.

  • Work with Growth to test formats and learn what people watch, share, and respond to.

  • Shoot and edit end to end, from capturing footage in the lab to the final cut.

  • Run the content calendar and keep a steady flow of work going out across our channels.

  • Capture the real moments of building a humanoid, the wins and the messy in-progress ones.

What We Look For

  • Hands-on video production and editing skills, with the judgment to know when a quick clip or a larger production is needed

  • A strong sense of story, pacing, and what works on each platform

  • Initiative to find stories and produce work without waiting for a detailed brief

  • An AI-native approach. You keep up with new models and tools, test them, and use what improves your work

  • A portfolio that shows you can make people feel something, not just a reel of clean edits

  • Comfort working fast in public at an early-stage company where things change week to week

Nice to Have

This is the most generalist role on the team. You set the direction, you connect the dots, and you are just as comfortable writing the narrative as you are running the plan behind it.

What You'll Do

  • Own the overall marketing strategy and turn the company roadmap into a story worth telling

  • Drive key partnerships that expand our reach, credibility, and distribution

  • Own press and media relations, and act as a trusted external voice for Menlo

  • Keep marketing aligned with product, business, and engineering, so the message always matches the machine

  • Set positioning and messaging for Asimov and the Menlo Platform

  • Build and prioritize the marketing roadmap, then decide what ships and what waits

  • Plan and run launches that make each milestone land

  • Measure what is working, kill what is not, and double down where it counts

  • Shape and grow the marketing team over time


What We Look For

  • A generalist marketer who has worn many hats and can move between strategy and execution without friction

  • A track record of owning marketing strategy and shipping launches that moved the needle

  • Real strength in partnerships and press, with the network and instincts to match

  • Credibility with engineers and researchers, and the ability to translate their work for the rest of the world

  • Comfort being the connective tissue across teams, keeping everyone pointed the same way

  • A bias to action and genuine comfort in an early-stage, fast-changing environment

  • Excellent writing and storytelling


Nice to Have

  • A background in deep tech, hardware, robotics, or AI

  • An existing press and partnership network you can activate on day one

  • Experience building a marketing function from close to zero

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Partner Solutions (Greece)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Mysten Labs believes that decentralized and open protocols are the bedrock of the internet of value. This is why at Mysten Labs, we are creating foundational infrastructure to accelerate the adoption of decentralized protocols based on blockchain technologies.

Mysten Labs Greece is seeking a Software Engineer to join our growing Solutions Engineering team in Greece! You will help design, develop, debug and deploy our next generation of decentralized applications.

Working closely with our senior engineers, you will receive training in smart contract development using the Move programming language and build applications that support blockchain developers and business partners worldwide. These include payment wallets, decentralized finance applications and agentic coordination systems.

AI coding tools and agents will be part of your development workflow, combining rapid experimentation with sound engineering judgment to deliver reliable software. You will also contribute to open source projects with global impact, collaborate with leading companies in blockchain and AI, and develop your expertise alongside experienced engineers.

This is a remote position requiring residence in Greece, with a strong preference for Athens or Thessaloniki. Occasional attendance at our Athens office is required.

What You'll Do:

  • Design, implement and test full stack applications, using AI coding agents to accelerate development while taking ownership of code quality, security and maintainability.

  • Work with (and travel as needed) international partners to onboard and port solutions to Sui.

  • Translate partner needs into clear technical requirements and rapidly build proof of concept applications that demonstrate how Sui can address real business problems.

  • Visualize and implement web UIs that improve the user experience for blockchain developers and partners.

  • Understand the capabilities of the Sui blockchain platform so that you can make use of its features and influence its evolution

  • Research blockchain technology and customers’ industries to inform technical decisions and proposed solution

Our Ideal Candidate Would Have:

  • Any degree in computer science or related field or/and experience in software engineering or equivalent work experience

  • 2+ years of industry software engineering experience

  • Experience with any of the following languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, Java or C#

  • Experience with any of the following UI Frameworks: React, Next.js, Vue

  • Practical experience using AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, including providing clear instructions, reviewing generated code and validating results through testing. Experience gained through personal or open source projects is welcome.

  • Understanding of relational databases and key value stores.

  • Experience in source code management tools, such as Git and GitHub

  • Strong collaboration, interpersonal, and verbal communication skills

  • Fluency in written and spoken English.

Experience with Rust or Solidity, and basic knowledge of distributed systems and architectures, would be a plus.


What We Offer

  • A highly competitive, top-of-market compensation package.

  • Best-in-class private health insurance, with coverage that goes well beyond what is typically offered in the Greek market.

  • A monthly wellness stipend to support your physical and mental well-being.

  • A flexible, remote-first working environment with flexible working hours, designed to support autonomy and close collaboration.

  • An AI-native engineering culture. We fully embrace AI-assisted development and invest heavily in leading AI tools, infrastructure, and resources.

  • Continuous mentorship, training, and hands-on learning alongside world-class engineers in blockchain, distributed systems, and AI.

  • Meaningful ownership of technically challenging products used by developers and business partners worldwide.

  • A fast-moving environment where experimentation is encouraged, engineering judgment is valued, and your work can have a visible impact.

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which may include verification of employment history, education credentials, criminal history, and other relevant information.

Regarding the recent rash of technology job scams: Be aware that emails from genuine Mysten Labs group recruiters will always come from the @mystenlabs.com domain or related subdomains (e.g., mystenlabs.com/careers). Remember: you can always verify positions on our job boards at www.mystenlabs.com/careers.

To support an efficient and fair hiring process, we may use technology-assisted tools, including artificial intelligence (AI), to help identify and evaluate candidates. All hiring decisions are ultimately made by human reviewers.

Our team is remote first and we are hiring across the world. Here at Mysten Labs, you’ll be joining a world-class team with tremendous growth potential as we bring the next billion users to web3. We raised a $300M Series B round from top Silicon Valley led venture funds like Jump Crypto, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Binance Labs, Redpoint, Lightspeed, Coinbase Ventures, Electric Capital, Standard Crypto, NFX, Slow Ventures, Scribble Ventures, Samsung Next, Lux Capital, among other investment firms and strategic partners. Come join us and build the future of web3!

jobs.title: Strategic Partnerships Dealmaker, Walrus
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Mysten Labs believes that decentralized and open protocols are the bedrock of the internet of value. This is why at Mysten Labs, we are creating foundational infrastructure to accelerate the adoption of decentralized protocols based on blockchain technologies.

The Role

We're hiring a Senior Partnerships Dealmaker to drive adoption of Walrus across the AI ecosystem. This is a frontline role. Your job is to:

  • Create opportunities by building new relationships with the platforms, enterprises, and standards bodies that matter most to Walrus.

  • Structure, negotiate, and close complex, non-template deals.

  • Develop deep expertise on our products, our target markets, and the impact of technology on our partners.

You'll work closely with the Head of Partnerships, who sets direction and strategy. You execute by identifying the right partners and getting deals done. Anything from a marketplace listing, to a flagship enterprise integration, to convening the players needed to create a new industry standard.

 
 

What You’ll Do:

  • Strategic Deal Making. Identify, engage, and build relationships with the players that matter most to Walrus's position in the market including hyperscalers and data platforms, AI builders and agentic-framework companies, data and compute vendors, and standards bodies. Build and manage a pipeline of high-leverage opportunities: marketplace listings, platform integrations, co-marketing, and standard-setting.

  • Ecosystem Positioning & Standards. Get Walrus Memory listed and ranked as a top memory provider where AI builders shop for infrastructure, and broker the relationships needed to shape emerging standards so that Walrus is designed in from the start as a viable solution for agentic workflows.

  • Strategy & Implementation. Identify critical external data points that help our leadership team develop a cohesive strategy across Partnerships, Product, and Marketing.

  • Deal Excellence. Lead intricate negotiations and contract discussions, ensuring terms are mutually advantageous and aligned with the strategic objectives of both parties.

  • Program Manage Deal Outcomes. Collaborate cross-functionally with internal stakeholders, taking an ownership approach to seeing a deal from signing through to integration and beyond.

What You’ll Have:

  • 7–10+ years in strategic partnerships, platform/ecosystem alliances, or corporate/business development at a data infrastructure, AI, or enterprise software company.

  • A track record of closing deals with large platforms or enterprises where you had to navigate multiple stakeholders and where the deal wasn't a simple sale

  • Technical curiosity. You aren't a data architect, but you can understand complex technical models, architectures, and agentic workflows.

  • Creative dealmaker. You have a strong, proven track record of constructing business relationships that don't follow a template.

  • You are passionate about decentralizing data infrastructure and the impact this has on the digital experience for everyone.

  • Curiosity about Web3 and decentralized infrastructure, and the ability to get fluent quickly. Prior crypto experience is a plus, not a requirement.

  • High ethical standards.

  • You appreciate direct communication.

  • You can pivot on the fly. What you worked on last month may not be what you work on today, and that excites you. You're not looking for a 9-to-5 job.

  • Ability to travel 20% or more of the time, often internationally.

jobs.title: Staff Security Engineer, Walrus
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Mysten Labs believes that decentralized and open protocols are the bedrock of the internet of value. This is why at Mysten Labs, we are creating foundational infrastructure to accelerate the adoption of decentralized protocols based on blockchain technologies.

The Role:

We are hiring a Staff Security Engineer to act as the primary security partner for the Walrus team, providing deep architectural guidance and embedding security practices throughout the development lifecycle, starting from the design phase.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead security assessments for new Walrus features while also contributing to security initiatives across the broader Mysten ecosystem, identifying systemic risks and providing actionable remediation plans for complex architectural challenges.

  • Drive a "security-by-design" culture, ensuring that security considerations are front-and-center before code is written, within Walrus and the wider Mysten organization.

  • Leverage AI-driven tools and advanced automation to identify and remediate low-hanging fruit, allowing the team to focus on high-impact, complex security research.

  • Maintain a generalist security perspective, providing strategic oversight on broader infrastructure and product security issues as they impact Walrus and beyond.

  • Collaborate with engineering leadership to prioritize security roadmap items, balancing feature velocity with the security posture of the platform.

  • Mentor senior and junior engineers, setting technical direction for security standards and establishing best practices across the engineering organization.



What You'll Have:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.

  • 8+ years of industry experience in security engineering, with a proven track record of operating at a Staff (E6) level or equivalent.

  • Extensive experience as a security generalist, capable of navigating infrastructure, application, and cryptographic security domains.

  • Strong proficiency in building, deploying, and managing automated security tooling; demonstrated history of using AI/ML or advanced static/dynamic analysis to improve security outcomes at scale.

  • Deep expertise in collaborating with engineering teams during the design phase to proactively identify and mitigate high-risk design flaws.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence technical direction and lead cross-functional security initiatives.



What You'll Have

Preferred Qualifications

  • Technical understanding of decentralized storage, distributed systems, or the Web3 stack (prior experience is a plus, not a requirement).

  • Experience leading security-focused transformations or implementing security-by-design frameworks in high-growth engineering environments.

  • Ability to balance tactical, hands-on security work with strategic long-term planning and leadership.

jobs.title: Associate General Counsel, Corporate
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Mysten Labs believes that decentralized and open protocols are the bedrock of the internet of value. This is why at Mysten Labs, we are creating foundational infrastructure to accelerate the adoption of decentralized protocols based on blockchain technologies.

We are building a world-class team of lawyers and legal professionals who serve as strategic partners to the business. We are looking for an experienced corporate attorney to join Mysten Labs and take ownership of a broad range of corporate legal matters.

Reporting to the General Counsel, you will work closely with leaders across the company on corporate governance, strategic transactions and investments, corporate structuring, finance, tax, employment and compensation matters, and other strategic initiatives. This is a broad, hands-on role for someone who enjoys solving novel problems, operating with significant autonomy, and taking ownership of matters from initial strategy through execution.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical corporate training with practical business judgment and the versatility to tackle matters that do not fit neatly within a single legal discipline.

Responsibilities

  • Lead and support strategic transactions, including joint ventures, strategic investments, acquisitions, dispositions, spinouts, restructurings and other complex corporate transactions.

  • Advise the General Counsel, executive team and other business leaders on corporate legal matters and strategic initiatives.

  • Work cross-functionally with finance, tax, accounting, people and other teams to structure and execute strategic corporate initiatives.

  • Advise on corporate finance and treasury matters, including equity and debt financings and other capital-related transactions.

  • Partner with the People team on employment, executive compensation, equity and token compensation, and other employee-related matters, coordinating with specialist counsel as appropriate.

  • Support the company’s international operations and corporate structure, including formation and governance of subsidiaries and other entities.

  • Draft, review and negotiate transaction documents, corporate agreements, Board and stockholder materials, policies and other legal documentation.

  • Identify legal and business risks, develop practical solutions, and communicate clear recommendations to senior stakeholders, often in situations involving novel issues or incomplete information.

  • Manage outside counsel and other external advisors efficiently, including determining when specialist expertise is necessary and driving matters toward resolution.

  • Develop and improve corporate legal processes, policies, templates and systems as the company continues to evolve.

  • Stay informed regarding legal and industry developments relevant to Mysten Labs and the broader web3 ecosystem.

  • Take on other legal and strategic projects as needed. We are a lean team, and everyone is expected to be willing to tackle important problems that fall outside their traditional lane.

  • Do whatever needs to be done, and do the right thing.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of relevant legal experience, including significant experience at a leading law firm and/or in the legal department of a high-growth technology company.

  • Strong foundation in corporate law, with meaningful experience in corporate governance and complex corporate transactions.

  • Experience with some combination of M&A, joint ventures, strategic investments, corporate restructurings, financings, subsidiary governance or other strategic corporate matters.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex matters, coordinate cross-functional stakeholders, and drive projects from initial issue identification through execution.

  • Ability and willingness to operate as a corporate generalist and quickly develop expertise in unfamiliar areas.

  • Excellent business judgment and the ability to assess and appropriately weigh legal and business risk, including when operating with imperfect information.

  • Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to distill complex issues into clear, actionable and practical advice.

  • Highly collaborative, solutions-oriented and comfortable working with stakeholders across finance, tax, accounting, people, operations and other functions.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Mysten Labs believes that decentralized and open protocols are the bedrock of the internet of value. This is why at Mysten Labs, we are creating foundational infrastructure to accelerate the adoption of decentralized protocols based on blockchain technologies.

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead engineers building wallet and DeFi experiences for the Sui ecosystem. This person will support Slush, Mysten Labs' wallet available across web, browser extension, iOS, and Android, and will help shape how users discover, understand, and execute onchain actions.

You will own team health and engineering outcomes for a product where errors can affect user assets and trust. You will partner with product, design, security, protocol, and ecosystem teams to set direction, make sound technical tradeoffs, and ship dependable experiences. You should have direct experience building wallets and be an active, informed DeFi user.

What You Will Do

  • Lead, hire, coach, and retain a team of engineers working across wallet clients, supporting services, and onchain integrations.

  • Set technical direction with senior engineers for account creation and recovery, key management, signing, transaction construction and simulation, dApp connectivity, asset management, swaps, and other DeFi experiences.

  • Create clear ownership and execution plans across web, browser extension, iOS, Android, backend services, SDKs, and protocol dependencies.

  • Raise standards for architecture, testing, release safety, observability, incident response, and post-incident learning in an asset-sensitive product.

  • Partner with product and design to simplify complex onchain workflows without hiding material fees, permissions, risks, or transaction outcomes from users.

  • Work with security and protocol teams to evaluate threats, manage dependencies, and make informed tradeoffs between usability, decentralization, privacy, and protection of user assets.

  • Use data, user research, support feedback, and ecosystem context to prioritize work and measure product and engineering outcomes.

What You Bring

  • Experience managing and developing software engineers, including senior engineers, in a high-ownership product environment.

  • Direct experience shipping production blockchain wallet functionality. You understand self-custody, private-key security, signing, recovery, transaction lifecycle, chain and RPC failure modes, and wallet-to-dApp interaction patterns.

  • Hands-on DeFi fluency. You regularly use onchain products and can reason about liquidity, routing, slippage, staking, lending, bridges, protocol and smart-contract risk, and the user protections required for financial transactions.

  • Strong systems judgment across client applications, backend services, APIs or SDKs, distributed dependencies, monitoring, and operational response.

  • A record of setting direction in ambiguous environments, improving execution, and delivering reliable products across multiple platforms or surfaces.

  • Ability to partner closely with product, design, security, and senior technical leaders while maintaining clear engineering accountability.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience integrating decentralized exchanges, aggregators, bridges, staking, lending, or fiat on- and off-ramps into a wallet.

  • Familiarity with Sui, Move, programmable transaction blocks, zkLogin, Wallet Standard, or another modern smart-contract platform.

jobs.title: Staff Product Designer, DeFi
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Mysten Labs believes that decentralized and open protocols are the bedrock of the internet of value. This is why at Mysten Labs, we are creating foundational infrastructure to accelerate the adoption of decentralized protocols based on blockchain technologies.

Mysten Labs is looking for a Staff Product Designer to set the experience strategy for the DeepBook financial stack and the first-party products built around it, spanning spot trading, margin, prediction markets, liquidity, and the workflows that connect users and builders to onchain finance on Sui.

This role requires strong product judgment, exceptional design craft, people leadership, and real fluency in financial markets and DeFi. You will work with product and engineering from strategy through launch, build a design team that can cover a growing product surface, and stay close enough to the work to lead critical product flows yourself.

The right person knows how to make complex financial systems clear without removing the information users need to assess risk. You should be comfortable designing for retail and professional users, working through technical and regulatory constraints, and using research and product data to improve adoption, execution quality, retention, and trust.

What You Will Do

  • Set the design vision, principles, and priorities in partnership with product, engineering, and business leadership.

  • Own the end-to-end experience across DeepBook spot, margin, prediction products, liquidity workflows, and related first-party applications.

  • Lead the design of core journeys including onboarding, funding, market discovery, order entry, transaction review and signing, portfolio and position management, collateral, liquidation risk, settlement, and recovery from failed states.

  • Design for distinct audiences such as retail traders, experienced DeFi users, market makers, liquidity providers, institutions, and developers without creating a fragmented product experience.

  • Remain hands-on in the highest-priority work by framing problems, developing concepts, prototyping, testing, and reviewing implementation quality.

  • Build a scalable design system and shared interaction patterns for dense financial data, charts, tables, order entry, account states, alerts, and risk communication.

  • Establish a practical research program using interviews, usability studies, product analytics, support feedback, and market observation.

  • Partner with engineering to understand protocol behavior, transaction states, latency, data dependencies, security boundaries, and platform constraints.

  • Work with legal, security, marketing, business development, and ecosystem teams to launch products responsibly and communicate financial concepts accurately.

  • Define design and product quality measures, then connect the team's work to activation, conversion, trading success, retention, support burden, and user trust.

What You Will Have

  • 10 or more years of product design experience, including meaningful experience leading, hiring, and developing designers in a fast-moving product organization.

  • A portfolio that shows both exceptional individual craft and leadership impact across complex, data-dense products.

  • Experience designing trading, investing, fintech, payments, crypto, marketplace, or other high-stakes products where users make consequential decisions.

  • Fluency in DeFi and direct experience using onchain products. You can discuss swaps, order books, liquidity, routing, slippage, collateral, leverage, liquidation, settlement, smart-contract risk, and transaction signing.

  • Strong product judgment and a record of shaping strategy, prioritization, and product decisions with product and engineering partners.

  • Skill in interaction design, information architecture, visual design, prototyping, research, and systems thinking.

  • Experience building design systems and operating practices that improve consistency and delivery across multiple products.

  • Comfort working through ambiguity and making progress while product, technical, market, and legal inputs continue to change.

Nice to Have

  • Experience leading design for an exchange, order book, derivatives or margin product, prediction market, wallet, aggregator, or institutional trading platform.

  • Experience with both retail and professional trading experiences, including charts, market data, portfolio analytics, and execution workflows.

  • Familiarity with Sui, Move, programmable transaction blocks, DeepBook, Slush, or object-based blockchain architectures.

  • Experience designing products in legally complex or regulated financial categories.

  • Prior experience as a founder, design executive, principal designer, trader, DeFi power user, or ecosystem operator.

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which may include verification of employment history, education credentials, criminal history, and other relevant information.
